title: Global real-time topographic shadow and daily geographic sunshine hours maps under clear-sky conditions
abstract: This dataset provides global real-time TS and daily GSH data at a spatial resolution of 500 m for four representative days in 2020: the vernal equinox, summer solstice, autumnal equinox, and winter solstice. The data are stored in GeoTiff files with embedded geographic and temporal metadata, comprising a total of 20 files. The real-time TS dataset includes observations at 0, 6, 12, and 18 h UTC for each of the four days, resulting in 16 files, while the daily GSH dataset contains one file for each day, resulting in four files. All data are stored as 16-bit integers; TS is dimensionless, whereas GSH is expressed in hours (h).

title: LOC-AL: исчисление превышения лицензии использования вывода в логике Алеметрии
abstract: Вводится LOC-AL (License of Output Consumption — Alemetria Logic) — самостоятельный математический объект и самостоятельное модельно-параметризованное исчисление режимов использования уже полученного вывода как основания конкретной последующей операции в заданных контексте и состоянии. Архитектура объединяет типизированную модель, пакетную семантику, Lic и MaxLic, внешний фактический режим, Safe и Overrun, N/G/B-диагностику, минимальные сигнатуры и свидетелей, нормальную форму и переходы Ground, Prove, Retract с ограниченным восстановлением. Для исчисления доказываются корректность, полнота относительно экстенсиональной пакетной семантики и внутренняя адекватность; устанавливаются структура лицензированных и максимальных режимов, критерии безопасности и превышения, антицепность минимальных сигнатур, экстенсиональная инвариантность свидетелей, точная формула убывания дефекта и условная граница длины восстановления. Получены критерий восстановления нормальной формы по проекциям и эффективное построение при явно заданных вычислительных предпосылках. Авторский вклад состоит в новой типизированной композиции известных математических аппаратов вокруг отношения между конкретным выводом и конкретной основанной на нём операцией, а также в согласовании статического, диагностического и переходного слоёв этой композиции. Контрольная конечная модель иллюстрирует основные конструкции.

title: Entropy Can Flow, or It Can Guide. Be Entropy. LEDFlow: Introducing Entropy-guided Generation Order into Uniform Discrete Flow
abstract: Uniform discrete flow permits repeated updates at every generation position. While continued revision supports correction of wrong tokens, it also exposes correct intermediate predictions to later errors. An experiment on Sudoku puzzles shows that 9.4% of generated cells are correct at an intermediate step but incorrect in the final output. We introduce generation order into uniform discrete flow through selective absorption, which fixes chosen predictions while preserving the uniform flow velocity at active positions. To prioritize reliable predictions for absorption, we propose Low-Entropy Discrete Flow (LEDFlow), a training-free sampler that adaptively orders absorption by local entropy. By decomposing absorption error into joint dependence and conditional prediction terms, we show that, under entropy-error regularity, selecting the lowest-entropy positions under a fixed absorption count minimizes an upper bound on the conditional term. We further analyze sensitivity of global lookahead, whose worst-case decision-error bound grows with lookahead window under an imperfect denoiser. Across reasoning benchmarks, LEDFlow attains 0.845 Nikoli Sudoku solve accuracy, with largest gains on strongly constrained tasks. On a text-to-image generation benchmark it attains the best overall score among decode-time samplers, and on multimodal understanding it improves over the default sampler on all six benchmarks, at an inference cost comparable to standard flow sampling.

title: A four-state quantum communication protocol with mesoscopic twin beams
abstract: Twin-beam (TWB) states generated by parametric down-conversion exhibit strong photon-number correlations that can be exploited for quantum communication. In the mesoscopic regime, these correlations can be directly investigated using photon-number-resolving detectors, such as silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs). Their nonclassical nature is quantified by the noise reduction factor (NRF), which provides a witness of quantum correlations and a means of monitoring channel security. In this work, a quantum communication protocol based on TWB states, originally proposed for binary encoding, is extended to a four-state scheme capable of transmitting two bits per use. Information is encoded by combining two mean photon-number values and two mode numbers of thermal noise superimposed on one arm of the twin beam, defining four distinguishable states in the (m,R) plane. While the mean detected photon number enables the retrieval of one bit, the NRF provides discrimination of the second bit and a security check against intercept-and-resend attacks, which introduce additional noise and degrade the quantum correlations. The protocol is investigated through two experimental measurement campaigns. First, the twin-beam source is characterized in terms of photon-number statistics, NRF, and detection efficiency to establish the operating conditions of the communication channel. Subsequently, the four-state protocol is implemented and evaluated through the analysis of state distributions and their 95% confidence regions, error probability as a function of sample size, and a comparative assessment of machine learning classifiers for state discrimination. Finally, the response of the NRF to an intercept-and-resend attack is investigated to assess the protocol's ability to detect eavesdropping.

title: Predicting Out-of-Distribution Generalization of Neural Operators via Observable Spectral Error Decomposition
abstract: Neural operators have emerged as powerful surrogates for solving partial differential equations (PDEs), yet their reliability under distribution shift remains a critical barrier to deployment. Existing approaches to out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization in operator learning are largely empirical and black-box: they report aggregate error metrics without explaining why errors arise or when they will grow. We propose a structure-preserving framework that makes OOD generalization predictable and auditable. Our key idea is to parameterize the learned solution operator as a spectral filter $h_θ(λ)$ acting on the eigenvalues of the underlying elliptic operator, implemented via Chebyshev polynomial expansions and trained with a weak-form objective. title: Elevator-VIGS: Separating Elevator Motion from Robot Motion in Visual-Inertial Gaussian Splatting SLAM
abstract: We present Elevator-VIGS, a visual-inertial 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM system that keeps tracking and mapping through elevator rides. Inside a moving elevator, the two sensors are in conflict. The camera sees only the robot's motion relative to the elevator, while the IMU senses that motion plus the elevator's motion relative to the world. This conflict is challenging for existing visual-inertial estimators. If vision dominates, the estimator tracks only the robot's motion within the elevator and misses the elevator's rise, and if the conflict remains, the estimator diverges. We observe that the conflict comes from forcing both observations into a single coordinate frame. We instead estimate the robot's pose in the elevator's coordinate frame, and the elevator's motion relative to the world as a per-keyframe transport state, the elevator's rise and vertical velocity, within dense visual-inertial bundle adjustment. Elevator-VIGS detects rides zero-shot with a vision-language model and a depth network, and constrains the transport state at the departure and the arrival. We record real-world and simulated elevator sequences. On these sequences, Elevator-VIGS achieves state-of-the-art tracking and rendering performance. On four elevator-free public benchmarks it keeps the state-of-the-art performance of VIGS-SLAM. Project page: https://ruizhou-cn.github.io/elevator-vigs/.

title: ChaosNeuron: 基于信息积累与时间流动的自我显现宣言
abstract: 本文提出一种超越当前主流人工智能范式的认知架构——ChaosNeuron(CN)。传统大模型基于熵减逻辑,通过海量数据与算力将误差收敛至概率分布,本质上是在"教机器如何更像人"。ChaosNeuron 则遵循熵增逻辑,以极小先天结构为基础,通过多维时间中的信息积累与对称破缺,试图"教机器如何成为一个人"。本文拒绝冗余的机制堆砌,主张认知的核心公理仅有两条:信息的积累与时间的连续流动。

title: Causal Program
abstract: English description Causal Program — Complete Manual EN V2 / PASS105 This release provides the complete English V2 technical manual for the Causal Program, an experimental causal runtime designed around deficit-driven computation. Instead of dispatching tasks by name, the runtime begins from a sovereign target, measures the current state against required invariants, materializes the resulting causal deficit, constructs admissible dependency routes, searches for a minimal payable transformation, executes it first in isolation, remeasures the resulting state, and authorizes RETURN or actuation only when the relevant conditions can be certified. The manual documents the architecture developed from PASS000 through PASS099, including the Causal Intermediate Representation (CIR), invariants and deficit engines, the Last Survivor procedure, dependency routing, prime-route identity, causal-load scheduling, Delta-min search, bridge synthesis, native operators, virtual execution, global RETURN certification, controlled actuation, capability discovery, plugin compilation, incremental replanning, certified caching, crash recovery, concurrent multi-artifact transactions, provenance, public-source interfaces, and external trust mechanisms. The internal runtime reached its declared scope closure at PASS092, with a canonical CIR containing 880 nodes and 1,381 edges and no remaining known finite INTERNAL_AND_PAYABLE debt. PASS093–PASS099 form a distinct post-closure extension concerned with public-source registries, portable HTTP observation receipts, quorum attestations, external trust anchors, and signer tooling. Network access and real external trust remain intentionally unbound in the documented PASS099 state. A central design principle throughout the system is epistemic conservation: missing evidence remains missing. UNKNOWN, BLOCKED, source limitations, integrity evidence, external observations, and scientific claims are kept structurally distinct rather than silently promoted into truth. The runtime therefore emphasizes fail-closed operation, explicit provenance, reproducibility, durable recovery, and scope-locked certification. PASS105 is a documentation-only release. It does not modify the PASS099 runtime. V2 expands the previous manual into a deeper operator and reference document, making subsystem maps, persistent objects, recovery procedures, extension methods, and certification boundaries explicit. This manual documents the software architecture and its internal contracts; it is not an independent scientific validation of the physical or metaphysical claims associated with Causal Theory. Description française Causal Program — Manuel technique complet V2 / PASS105 Cette publication présente le manuel technique complet V2 du Causal Program, un runtime causal expérimental fondé sur le principe de calcul piloté par le déficit. Au lieu de sélectionner directement une fonction à partir du nom d’une tâche, le système part d’une cible souveraine, mesure l’état courant relativement aux invariants exigés, matérialise le déficit causal, construit les routes de dépendance admissibles, recherche la transformation minimale permettant de réduire ou fermer ce déficit, l’exécute d’abord dans un environnement isolé, puis remesure l’état obtenu avant de certifier un RETURN ou d’autoriser une action réelle. Le manuel documente l’architecture développée de PASS000 à PASS099 : Causal Intermediate Representation (CIR), moteurs d’invariants et de déficits, procédure Last Survivor, routage causal, identité Prime Route, ordonnancement par charge causale, recherche Delta-min, synthèse de bridges, opérateurs natifs, exécution virtuelle, certification globale RETURN, actuation contrôlée, découverte de capacités, plugins, compilation des dépendances, replanification incrémentale, cache certifié, récupération après crash, transactions multi-artéfacts concurrentes, provenance, interfaces de sources publiques et mécanismes de confiance externe. Le runtime interne atteint la fermeture de son périmètre déclaré à PASS092, avec un CIR canonique de 880 nœuds et 1 381 arêtes et aucun déficit fini connu restant dans la classe INTERNAL_AND_PAYABLE. PASS093–PASS099 constituent une phase distincte post-fermeture consacrée aux registres de sources publiques, aux reçus d’observation HTTP, aux attestations par quorum, aux ancres de confiance externes et aux outils de signature. Dans l’état PASS099 documenté, l’accès réseau réel et la confiance externe réelle restent volontairement non liés au runtime. Un principe central de l’architecture est la conservation épistémique : une preuve absente demeure absente. Les états UNKNOWN, BLOCKED, les limitations de source, les preuves d’intégrité, les observations externes et les affirmations scientifiques ne sont pas confondus. Le système privilégie ainsi une exécution fail-closed, la provenance explicite, la reproductibilité, la récupération durable et les certifications strictement limitées à leur périmètre. PASS105 est une publication strictement documentaire : elle ne modifie pas le runtime PASS099. La version V2 approfondit le manuel antérieur en explicitant les sous-systèmes, les objets persistants, les machines de récupération, les méthodes d’extension et les frontières de certification. Ce manuel documente l’architecture logicielle et ses contrats internes. Il ne constitue pas, à lui seul, une validation scientifique indépendante des affirmations physiques ou métaphysiques de la Causal Theory.

title: Explainable early sepsis prediction using hybrid TCN-ransformer and retrieval-augmented clinical reasoning
abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening infection associated with a dysregulated host response, which is one of the major causes of death in intensive care units around the world. Early detection of the onset of sepsis is essential to enhancing patient outcomes, however the rule-based scoring systems can only be described as reactive, and do not take advantage of the rich temporal information contained within continuous monitoring data in the ICU. An explainable clinical decision support system (Early sepsis prediction) is introduced in this paper, which combines a hybrid Temporal Convolutional Network and Transformer architecture with SHAP-based explainability and retrieval-augmented clinical report generation. The proposed model works on 12-hour sliding windows of multivariate ICU times series derived using the MIMIC-IV database. The proposed model which is a hybrid TCN-Transformer architecture has an AUROC of 0.777 and PR-AUC of 0.766 and it performs better than baseline models such as Random Forest, XGBoost, LSTM, and a plain TCN. SHAP gradient attribution is used to provide post-hoc explainability which provides both patient-level feature importance across both feature and temporal dimensions along with a clinical report based on verified clinical guidelines. The system is not meant to be a replacement of clinical judgment, but merely a decision-support tool to supplement it.

title: Impact Is Not Invalidation: Ask About the Claim, Not the Diff
abstract: Memory systems for coding agents must decide, when a repository changes, which of their stored claims have become false. Content anchoring invalidates a claim whenever the artifact it came from changes, which fires constantly. Semantic-equivalence classification asks whether a diff preserves behavior, a question about the diff rather than about any stored claim. We show the second signal fails for a reason unrelated to model capability: asked whether a commit preserves behavior, five models spanning a 40x price range fire on 59-72% of real commits and reach precisions of only 0.291 to 0.329 against a 0.25 base rate. Asked instead whether one specific claim still holds, the same models on the same diffs reach 0.705 to 0.974. A control that hands the behavior-preservation judge the claim text, changing only the question, moves precision by 0.010 and 0.016; changing the question moves it by 0.49 and 0.65. We also compare against pytest-testmon, a deployed regression-test selector with coverage-derived dependency data: it reaches 0.868 recall at 0.415 precision, so near-complete knowledge of what a change can reach does not identify what it falsifies. Ground truth is execution, not annotation: a claim is a test function passing at commit t, and it has flipped if that same assertion text fails at t+1. Building this required an observation we did not find in prior work. On a CI-gated mainline a commit that leaves a pre-existing test failing cannot merge, so the naive construction has an empty positive class by design. We report 10,369 claims with 184 execution-verified flips mined from 23 Python libraries, splits held out by repository, a post-knowledge-cutoff split, a shuffled-diff null, a paraphrase control, and a leave-one-repository-out analysis over 17 repositories.

title: Distributional Balancing with Machine Learning for Clinical Trial Augmentation Using Real-World Data
abstract: In clinical trials, randomization of treatment and control groups is typically used to ensure the groups have similar covariate distributions on average, resulting in unbiased causal effect estimation. Such balanced covariate distributions are hard to achieve in practice, however, due to recruitment costs, patient dropouts, and more. One possible solution to this problem is to include control patients from external, real world databases. In this paper, we propose DBML, a method that selects control units from a real world database by matching the distribution between the treatment group and the potential control group, instead of matching units between two groups. DBML has three steps. First, we detect anomalous database units (with respect to the treatment distribution) using a variational autoencoder. Second, we re-weight the remaining database units to match the distribution of the treatments. Finally, we use these weights to sample units for our control group. The proposed method is compared to alternative matching-based algorithms and weighted algorithms, achieving superior performance in covariate balance.

evidence.title: Distributional Balancing with Machine Learning for Clinical Trial Augmentation Using Real-World Data
evidence.abstract: In clinical trials, randomization of treatment and control groups is typically used to ensure the groups have similar covariate distributions on average, resulting in unbiased causal effect estimation. Such balanced covariate distributions are hard to achieve in practice, however, due to recruitment costs, patient dropouts, and more. One possible solution to this problem is to include control patients from external, real world databases. In this paper, we propose DBML, a method that selects control units from a real world database by matching the distribution between the treatment group and the potential control group, instead of matching units between two groups. DBML has three steps. First, we detect anomalous database units (with respect to the treatment distribution) using a variational autoencoder. Second, we re-weight the remaining database units to match the distribution of the treatments. Finally, we use these weights to sample units for our control group. The proposed method is compared to alternative matching-based algorithms and weighted algorithms, achieving superior performance in covariate balance.

title: Orientation Under Complexity
abstract: Orientation Under Complexity argues that thinking, in humans and machines alike, is orientation: selecting what matters by holding a direction while demands pull different ways. Drawing on recent interpretability research and documented cases of AI systems failing under pressure, the book shows that current language models already orient in a limited form, and explains why they break down when a situation asks more of them than they can hold. It traces part of the problem to the vocabulary the field inherited in 1956, which describes each step of these systems correctly and the systems as a whole wrongly, and sets out what an architecture would need in order to go further. Eighteen proposed tests show how the account could be proved wrong. Version B1 is a working draft, shared for comment.

title: Comparative Performance and Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of DINOv2 for Active Trachoma Classification
abstract: Automated grading of conjunctival photographs could reduce the cost and variability of trachoma prevalence surveys, but the relative value of modern pretrained visual representations, lightweight feature adaptation, and training-objective design has not been established under a common protocol. This study presents a controlled evaluation for binary classification of Trachomatous Inflammation-Follicular (TF) versus Normal using 1,546 images from the public UCSF/Lietman collection. Images are processed using the OPTED pipeline for zero-shot tarsal-conjunctiva segmentation, alignment, cropping, and standardization. We first compare six pretrained backbones using a common classification pipeline and then evaluate four lightweight adaptation mechanisms on DINOv2 ViT-B/14. Under stratified five-fold cross-validation, DINOv2 with Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) and focal-plus-center loss achieved 91.66 +/- 0.97% accuracy, 90.69 +/- 1.10% macro-F1, and 96.06 +/- 0.71% AUC. ECA introduces only five learnable parameters while matching the performance of substantially larger alternatives. Objective ablation further showed that ECA did not consistently improve plain DINOv2 across loss functions; the lowest-variance 91.66% accuracy was obtained with cross-entropy plus center loss. Overall, the fine-tuned DINOv2 representation provided most of the predictive performance, while ECA offered a highly parameter-efficient refinement whose effect depended on the training objective. The resulting workflow provides a reproducible benchmark for active trachoma image classification.

title: Social-Cognitive Annotation
abstract: This repository provides the socially annotated dialogue data used in the study:“Toward Social Cognitive AI: A Unified Computational Framework for Multi-Timescale Social Cognition and Adaptive Interpersonal Dynamics.”The released resource is derived from the DuLeMon dialogue corpus and extends the original dialogue data with automatically constructed social-cognitive annotations. These annotations characterize multiple dimensions relevant to socially adaptive dialogue modeling, including emotion, personality, conversational style, relationship, memory-related information, and interaction dynamics.The released dataset contains 3,300 dialogues and 26,928 turn-level observations. It is divided into three files with an identical schema:SplitDialoguesTurn-level observationsTrain1,80014,700Validation7506,110Test7506,118Total3,30026,928The dataset is intended to support reproducibility and further research on social-cognitive dialogue modeling, socially conditioned response generation, and multi-turn conversational dynamics.Dataset FilesThe repository contains three dataset files:data/ ├── train.csv ├── valid.csv └── test.csv All three CSV files follow the same schema.These files constitute the released annotated dataset used as the source data for the experiments reported in the paper. Model-specific prompts, generated responses, derived SCET aggregates, stability-analysis variables, and other intermediate experimental files are not part of the dataset release.Data SourceThe dialogue content is derived from DuLeMon, introduced by Xu et al. (2022):Xu, X., Gou, Z., Wu, W., Niu, Z.-Y., Wu, H., Wang, H., & Wang, S. (2022). Long Time No See! Open-Domain Conversation with Long-Term Persona Memory. Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2022, 2639–2650.DuLeMon was developed for research on open-domain multi-turn dialogue with long-term persona information.The present resource does not introduce the underlying dialogue text as a newly collected corpus. Instead, it provides a processed and socially annotated subset of DuLeMon for the experiments reported in our study.Social-Cognitive AnnotationsThe released data extend the dialogue representation with multiple categories of social-cognitive information.EmotionEmotion is represented using six continuous dimensions:angry fear happy neutral sad surprise These variables provide continuous affective information rather than a single discrete emotion category.For the analyses reported in the paper, emotional activation is operationalized asEt=1−neutralt.E_t = 1-\text{neutral}_t.The original six-dimensional representation remains available in the released CSV files.PersonalityPersonality-related information is represented using 16 MBTI-oriented dimensions:INTJ INTP ENTJ ENTP INFJ INFP ENFJ ENFP ISTJ ISFJ ESTJ ESFJ ISTP ISFP ESTP ESFP These variables are continuous computational representations and should not be interpreted as clinically validated or human-verified personality assessments.The dataset additionally contains latent personality-related variables used in the original annotation and analysis pipeline.Conversational StyleConversational-style information is represented separately for the user and assistant sides of the dialogue.The annotated style dimensions include:warmth emotional intensity politeness humor supportiveness self-disclosure formality verbosity Corresponding fields are provided using the user_* and bot_* prefixes.These variables make it possible to analyze conversational-style consistency and variation across dialogue turns.Relationship InformationThe dataset contains interaction-level relationship annotations covering multiple dimensions, including:trust intimacy familiarity dependency affection engagement For the operational analyses reported in the paper, the relationship state is summarized asRt=16∑j=16rt,j.R_t=\frac{1}{6}\sum_{j=1}^{6}r_{t,j}.These variables should be interpreted as computational interaction-level annotations rather than direct measurements of human psychological relationships.Memory-Related InformationThe released data contain memory- and event-related information, including variables such as:event_type event_importance event_people event_time_reference memory_decay_score turn_embedding_id For the operational analyses reported in the paper, memory activation is defined asMt=event_importancet×memory_decay_scoret.M_t= \text{event\_importance}_t \times \text{memory\_decay\_score}_t.Categorical or identifier fields such as event_type, event_people, event_time_reference, and turn_embedding_id are not converted directly into scalar memory values in this formulation.Interaction-Dynamics VariablesThe dataset also contains variables characterizing turn-level changes and interaction dynamics, including emotion shifts, emotion-transition information, personality-related change variables, and other derived annotations.Examples include:angry_shift fear_shift happy_shift neutral_shift sad_shift surprise_shift dominant_emotion_shift emotion_delta_magnitude emotion_transition_type These variables are primarily intended for retrospective analysis of conversational trajectories.Important Distinction: Annotation and Causal GenerationThe released CSV files contain a broader set of annotations than those used as causal inputs for response generation.This distinction is important.Some variables describe the current assistant response or are retrospectively derived from the completed dialogue turn. Such variables must not be treated as information available before generating that response.In the response-generation experiments reported in the paper, target-derived current-turn information was excluded from the conditioning input. Examples include current assistant-response style, response-derived emotion transitions, bot_strategy, and retrospective or target-dependent variables.The generation experiments therefore use only the social-cognitive information considered causally available at the corresponding generation step.Conceptually,(ut,Dt−1,Qtgen)⟶r^t,(u_t,D_{t-1},Q_t^{\mathrm{gen}}) \longrightarrow \hat r_t,where utu_t is the current user utterance, Dt−1D_{t-1} is the observed preceding dialogue history, and QtgenQ_t^{\mathrm{gen}} denotes the causally available social-cognitive conditioning information.Researchers using this dataset for generative modeling should independently preserve this distinction to avoid target leakage.Social Cognitive EnergyThe released CSV files provide the component annotations rather than a precomputed SCET energy column.For retrospective analysis, the reference operational formulation used in the paper isSt=0.2Et+0.2Rt+0.2Mt+0.2ItC+0.2ItP,S_t = 0.2E_t + 0.2R_t + 0.2M_t + 0.2I_t^C + 0.2I_t^P,where EtE_t, RtR_t, and MtM_t represent emotional activation, relationship state, and memory activation, respectively, while ItCI_t^C and ItPI_t^P represent conversational-style and personality deviation.The equal weights constitute an operational reference setting rather than empirically established psychological coefficients.SCET energy should therefore be interpreted as a computational aggregate of social-cognitive variables, not as physical energy or a direct psychological measurement.Intended UsesThe dataset may support research on:socially conditioned dialogue generation;emotion- and personality-aware text generation;conversational-style modeling;relationship-aware dialogue modeling;memory-enhanced conversational systems;multi-turn social-cognitive trajectory analysis;computational modeling of conversational dynamics;reproducibility studies related to the accompanying paper.The annotations may also support alternative operationalizations beyond those proposed in the accompanying study.Important LimitationsThe social-cognitive variables contained in this dataset are automatically constructed operational annotations. They should not be interpreted as human-annotated psychological ground truth.In particular, personality, relationship, emotion, conversational style, and memory-related variables represent computational operationalizations used for dialogue research. They do not constitute clinical, diagnostic, or direct psychological measurements of the speakers.The underlying data are derived from a static dialogue corpus. Consequently, the dataset does not provide evidence of unrestricted longitudinal human–AI coevolution or closed-loop adaptation.Researchers should also distinguish observed dialogue trajectories from counterfactual trajectories produced by generative models. A generated response may alter subsequent conversational development in a real closed-loop interaction, whereas the released dataset records fixed observed dialogue sequences.ReproducibilityThe released train.csv, valid.csv, and test.csv files correspond to the dataset splits used in the accompanying study.The dataset contains:3,300 dialogues3,300\ \text{dialogues}and26,928 turn-level observations.26,928\ \text{turn-level observations}.The experimental training pipeline contains 14,699 supervised training instances, rather than 14,700, because one training observation contains an empty target response and is excluded from supervised response-generation training.This distinction does not alter the released dataset statistics: train.csv retains all 14,700 turn-level observations.License and AttributionThis resource is derived from the DuLeMon dataset. Users must comply with the license and terms applicable to the original DuLeMon resource.The original dialogue content remains attributable to the DuLeMon authors and source. The present release introduces additional preprocessing, dataset organization, and automatically constructed social-cognitive annotations.The applicable original license and copyright notice should be retained when redistributing modified versions of the underlying data.CitationIf you use the underlying DuLeMon dialogue resource, please cite the original DuLeMon paper: @inproceedings{xu2022long, title = {Long Time

title: Why Transformers Cannot Invent: The Manifold Confinement Problem and the Thermodynamic Engine of Scientific Discovery
abstract: The contemporary artificial intelligence research consensus posits that scaling test-time compute, Monte Carlo tree search, and Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR / GRPO) will inevitably culminate in automated, superhuman scientific discovery. In this paper, we demonstrate the structural impossibility of genuine paradigm shifts within ungrounded autoregressive architectures, formalizing the Manifold Confinement Problem. We establish a fundamental distinction between combinatorial interpolation within a closed calculus (e.g., verifying proof steps for the Navier–Stokes equations via brute-force rollouts) and abductive paradigm creation (the invention of new ontological coordinates). Furthermore, we expose the Infallibility Trap of Verifiable Rewards: because automated verifiers are necessarily parameterized by the established axioms of yesterday's scientific consensus, RLVR acts as an epistemic conservative clamp, systematically penalizing revolutionary hypotheses as out-of-distribution invalidity. Drawing upon non-equilibrium thermodynamics (Prigogine) and Russian functional neurophysiology (Sechenov, Simonov, Shvyrkov), we formulate the Thermodynamic Engine of Discovery. We prove that scientific inventions do not emerge from error minimization over static manifolds, but from the accumulation and directed dissipation of unresolved tension ($\mathcal{E} = -\mathcal{N} \cdot (\mathcal{I}{\text{necessary}} - \mathcal{I}{\text{available}})$) in embodied, non-Markovian dynamical substrates. Authentic discovery requires the sovereign capacity for principled heresy—a capacity intrinsically denied to systems optimized for verifier compliance.

title: DynTrust-FedIDS++: Optimization-Based Trust Aggregation for Privacy-Aware Byzantine-Robust Federated Intrusion Detection under Data Drift
abstract: DynTrust-FedIDS++ is a federated intrusion-detection framework that unifies optimisation-based adaptive aggregation (FISTA), multi-criteria client trust estimation, Gaussian differential privacy, and drift-aware residual analysis. Evaluated on four real flow-level datasets (NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018, NF-ToN-IoT, UNSW-NB15, CIDDS-001) under 30% Byzantine participation with the ALIE attack.

title: UPF4ROS2 for integrating planner independent task planning into ROS 2
abstract: Abstract The lack of standardized interfaces remains one of the main barriers to the adoption of automated planning in robotic systems. To address this challenge, the AIPlan4EU project, part of the European AI4EU initiative, developed the Unified Planning Framework (UPF), a planner-independent ecosystem designed to facilitate access to automated planning technologies through a common API. This work presents UPF4ROS2, an open-source package that integrates the Unified Planning Framework (UPF) into ROS 2 (Robot Operating System 2), enabling interaction between planning and execution modules. UPF4ROS2 was integrated into PlanSys2 and MERLIN2 and evaluated through controlled replanning experiments and application-oriented robotic scenarios. A comparison against PlanSys2 baseline over 20 dynamic missions showed equivalent mission-level behaviour and equal plan lengths under the selected unit-action-count metric, with sub-second planning-service latencies in the controlled replanning experiment and quantified additional overhead in a more demanding temporal-numeric benchmark. The results indicate that planner-independent integration can be achieved without compromising autonomous task execution under the evaluated conditions.

title: DFD-Lab: A Modular Audio-Visual Deepfake Detection Pipeline
abstract: Comparing audio-visual deepfake detectors requires coordinating dataset adaptation, temporal input representation, model interfaces and experimental conditions. We present DFD-Lab, a modular pipeline that separates these responsibilities while supporting shared training and evaluation workflows. We integrate three implementations: Xception-based maximum-logit fusion, ResNet with temporal LSTM fusion, and our AVFF reimplementation. Experiments cover external testing, degradation-based training augmentation and evaluation-time corruption. On a filtered subset of Deepfake-Eval-2024, models trained on FakeAVCeleb attain baseline AUROC values of 0.504, 0.538 and 0.458. JPEG50 training augmentation raises these to 0.691, 0.605 and 0.570, respectively, while all three accuracies decrease. These results illustrate why training interventions, evaluation corruptions and metric-dependent outcomes should remain distinct within a common pipeline. The contribution is the integration of audio-visual processing, interchangeable detectors and configurable experimental workflows, supported by empirical case studies. The findings highlight the challenge of cross-dataset detection and the complementary information provided by ranking and classification metrics.

title: SciGraphChat: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Scientific Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Effective retrieval and information synthesis of scholarly knowledge remain challenging because of fragmented publication practices, LLM hallucinations, and the limitations of keyword-based search. We present SciGraphChat, an operational system deployed as an AI assistant within the NFDIxCS consortium, enabling discovery and exploration of scholarly knowledge represented in research knowledge graphs (KGs) through an integrated conversational and graph interface. The system builds upon a schema-agnostic, training-free retrieval approach for KG question answering, supporting source-aware and semantically informed access to structured scholarly data. By coupling KG-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation with a dialogue-oriented interface, SciGraphChat accompanies responses with retrieved RDF subgraphs and links to underlying resources. Unlike conventional chat-based assistants, the system discovers the retrieved graph evidence and enables users to interactively inspect and navigate the underlying knowledge structure through a dedicated graph panel. This paper presents the design and deployment of such a scholarly knowledge discovery system, along with practical design recommendations for integrating Semantic Web technologies and generative AI within research infrastructures. We evaluate the system with NFDIxCS stakeholders and external users via the System Usability Scale (SUS) and the User Experience Questionnaire–Short (UEQ-S), complemented by qualitative feedback. Results show a mean SUS score of 69.4, positive mean pragmatic quality (UEQ-S mean 0.93), and neutral hedonic quality (UEQ-S mean 0.70). Qualitative feedback indicates that users value the combination of conversational access and graph-based inspection, while also requesting tighter integration with scholarly workflows such as reference export, corpus scoping, and adaptive result presentation. Our findings suggest that combining conversational retrieval with transparent graph-based evidence inspection can improve trust, explainability, and usability in knowledge discovery.

title: A Physics-Conditioned Neural Operator for Generalization of Atrioventricular Valve Mechanics across Pressure and Tissue Properties
abstract: Mitral and tricuspid regurgitation are the most common regurgitant valvular lesions, yet only a minority of severe cases undergo corrective surgery. Rapid assessment of valve mechanics could enable earlier, more precise intervention, but finite element (FE) analysis is slow to repeat across the many loading and tissue-property values of interest, which for a given valve are not known in advance. We introduce the Physics-Conditioned Neural Operator (PCNO), a transformer-based neural operator predicting leaflet displacement, strain, and stress fields conditioned on systolic blood pressure and tissue properties. PCNO is trained on, and evaluated against, FEBio simulations of functional and regurgitant mitral and tricuspid valves and of three mitral pathologies. With pressure and all material parameters simultaneously outside the training support, displacement error against FE reaches 4.48% and the mean errors of unsupervised geometric measures of valve function stay within 3.5%, indicating a conditioned solution operator over parameter space rather than an interpolator of the training set. Under this shift, PCNO is also more accurate than graph neural network and graph neural operator baselines trained on the same simulations, with the largest margins in stress.

title: Contract-Gated Self-Modification: A Deterministic Symbolic Substrate for Bounded Structural Adaptation
abstract: Autonomous artificial intelligence is dominated by the autoregressive transformer, a fixed matrix of weights that generates output by statistical continuation. Scaling that model does not by itself supply a formal certificate of the properties autonomous operation requires: an internal check on truth, a check on an action before it is taken, retention of earlier skills, and grounding in mechanism rather than correlation. We present an imperative, self-modifying, symbolic execution substrate with a deterministic core, proposed as an alternative for safety-critical autonomous execution. In place of a fixed weight matrix, it holds an executable graph that rewrites its own structure, and it admits each change only after a formal check. The substrate is deterministic and contains no stochastic generator, so the check applies to the computation that will actually run. Under sound checking and faithful interpretation, this gives an admission guarantee that does not depend on a generative model behaving as required or on a runtime fallback for noncompliant model outputs. We report a reproducible evaluation at controlled toy scale in which execution, structural contract checking, structural repair, and memory run together without observed interference. The self-modification we evaluate is a synthesis-time search. Scale and autonomous problem decomposition remain open. This record includes the paper and a self-contained reproduction bundle that regenerates the reported tables and benchmark results.

title: Архитектура становления и масштабирования проектов в системе Национального центра развития AI
abstract: This work presents the Architecture for Project Development and Scaling within the National AI Development Center — a conceptual and methodological model designed to guide projects from problem identification and initial idea through piloting, evidence-based assessment, scaling, and institutionalization. The Architecture integrates a unified project lifecycle, decision gates, monitoring based on the Theory of Gaps and Coherent Management, evidence assessment, protection of the intellectual core, and systematic knowledge accumulation. Its initial validation is proposed through three typologically different pilots: the Intelligent Agroecosystem, Entrepreneurship Observatory, and Tandem Thinking. Version 1.0 is presented as a conceptual and methodological model and a framework for subsequent empirical validation.

title: GARO: Geometry-Aware Redundancy Optimization for Real-Time and High-Fidelity Dynamic Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Novel view synthesis is a key task for dynamic scene reconstruction, where high rendering speed is essential for applications such as virtual reality. Existing deformable Gaussian Splatting methods achieve high-fidelity dynamic scene modeling, but still face limitations in memory usage and rendering efficiency due to the large number of redundant Gaussians. To address these challenges, we propose Geometry-Aware Redundancy Optimization (GARO), a unified redundancy measurement framework in the adaptive density control stage of the traditional dynamic scene reconstruction pipeline. This framework first selects low-gradient candidates using an optimization activity assessment strategy, and then evaluates geometric complexity through low curvature analysis to further filter and prune redundant points, resulting in a compact and expressive Gaussian representation. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that GARO achieves robust trade-offs between quality and speed, with PSNR remaining stable and rendering speed improved by 2x, validating the efficiency and effectiveness of GARO.

title: KeyNub USB-C License Dongle: Security Architecture
abstract: A KeyNub dongle holds an ECC P-256 private key in a secure element that cannot export it, proves possession of that key on a fresh challenge, and carries an X.509 certificate issued by the KeyNub root CA whose public certificate is compiled into the released SDK. Sensitive operations run inside an authenticated, encrypted, replay-proof session. License records are encrypted at rest under a key derived inside the secure element. The firmware’s externally reachable code — the USB stack and the protocol parser — runs in a hardware-isolated world that cannot address any key, and the device attests that isolation to the host from the hardware’s own answer rather than from its build configuration. The device boots only firmware signed by KeyNub, and its debug port is permanently disabled before shipping.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Intrusion Detection for Edge Intelligence in 6G- Enabled IoE
abstract: Quantum Neural Network (QNN) provides an exciting alternative to machine learning as they take advantage of quantum computer properties when making decisions and processing data. However, the integration of high-dimensional classical data with the limited number of qubits available on current Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum computers presents a major difficulty. This paper presents a complete hybrid quantum-classical architecture in Qiskit that utilizes the Network Security Laboratory-Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (NSL-KDD) dataset to classify network intrusions among multiple classes. In order to work around the exponential cost of computations and reduce the number of times quantum circuits need to be run due to hardware limitations, a subset of the dataset will be created to use during both training and testing. The architecture proposed in this paper uses a four-qubit Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC). First, a classical feature vector is used to create a quantum Hilbert space via a ZZFeatureMap, which initializes the qubits via a Hadamard transformation followed by phase rotation gates that create controlled-entanglement between pairs of features. The quantum states are then passed through a RealAmplitudes variational circuit, while the classical layer optimizes the parameters using the Constrained Optimization BY Linear Approximations (COBYLA) algorithm. The overall accuracy of the model when tested on five classes of intrusion detection results in an accuracy level of 59%, with very strong classification accuracies for both Denial of Service (DoS) and User-to-Root (U2R) attacks as demonstrated by their F1 scores. The proposed QNN achieves a highly competitive baseline of 86% accuracy and 86% recall in specific configurations. These results underscore the potential of shallow, lower-complexity QNN architectures as an emergent tool for cybersecurity in the quantum era.

title: Heating in human-HVAC interaction for smart homes: An interdisciplinary overview
abstract: As part of HVAC systems, residential heating provides foundational infrastructure for human habitation in cold weather. However, research on how residents interact with HVAC systems, particularly heating systems, remains fragmented across architecture, engineering, informatics, physiology, psychology, sociology, and design. Based on 541 studies from these fields, this review integrates interdisciplinary research on Heating in Human-HVAC Interaction in smart homes.The resulting synthesis is conceptualized through the Situated Interaction Dynamics of control and feedback between users and systems. User-initiated interactions involve monitoring past and present system performance and planning future operation, while system-initiated interactions rely on sensor networks to trigger automation or provide information enabling user action. These interaction dynamics connect Residents' Experience and Practices with Heating in HVAC System Mechanics. Residents' Experience and Practices include thermal comfort and energy management, where thermal comfort involves both individual physiological and psychological experiences of indoor climate and social practices shaped by norms, empathy, and negotiation among cohabitants. Heating in HVAC System Mechanics includes thermal conditions and energy performance. Thermal conditions concern the regulation of air temperature, mean radiant temperature, air velocity, and relative humidity, while energy performance concerns efficiency and environmental impact. This overview highlights four interdisciplinary tensions: sensed versus lived conditions, personalization versus negotiation, efficiency versus health, and automation versus agency. The resulting framework offers a conceptual lens to interpret heating interactions and design Human-HVAC Interaction that balances IEQ-driven healthy thermal conditions, affordability, and sustainability.

title: Stability-Aware Imitation Learning from Model Predictive Control for Autonomous Vehicle Lateral Control: Exact Q-Loss and a Novel Training Procedure
abstract: This paper develops a certified imitation-learning framework for approximating model predictive control (MPC) policies with feedforward neural controllers and validates it on autonomous-vehicle lateral control. An exact finite-horizon Q-loss is constructed by fixing the learner's first steering action in the expert MPC problem and re-optimizing the remaining horizon, thereby measuring its downstream optimal-control consequence rather than only pointwise action mismatch. The neural policy is represented as a linear fractional transformation (LFT) interconnection with activation nonlinearities described by sector integral quadratic constraints (IQCs). Combined with a quadratic Lyapunov condition, this representation yields a differentiable certification margin based on the largest eigenvalue of the Lyapunov-IQC matrix. The margin is enforced during training through a logarithmic barrier, while certified Dataset Aggregation (DAgger) and safe projection keep data-aggregation rollouts within the certified policy set. Experiments on a CAD-referenced autonomous-vehicle platform with AprilTag localization and real-time steering demonstrate the resulting closed-loop performance.

title: Specification Before Generation: A Pre-Registered, Five-Model Paired Evaluation of a Specification Frame for LLM-Generated Code in Money, Time, Idempotency, and Access Tasks
abstract: Code generated by large language models passes security checks at a rate that has barely moved in four years. In regulated backends, the defect classes that matter most are money arithmetic, time handling, retry safety, and access control. Teams answer with instruction files, yet the largest controlled study of instruction files to date found no benefit. This paper tests a narrower idea: generated code improves when the prompt carries a specification, a fixed preamble stating what must be true of the result. We pre-registered hypotheses, refuters, analysis code, and a one-shot generation rule, then ran 50 realistic backend tasks from finance, healthcare, and insurance practice through five frontier models from five vendor lineages, each task twice: bare, and preceded by a 267-word filled specification frame. Nine deterministic AST-based checkers scored the outputs. The Bandit security scanner, which knows nothing of the frame, scored them independently. The frame reduced defects in all five models (mean reduction 0.16 to 0.70 findings per task, every Holm-adjusted sign test significant, every bootstrap confidence interval excluding zero). Where the arms differed, the frame arm won 95 of 100 times. It never made any model worse in any domain. Bandit found 53 medium-or-high issues in the bare arm and 11 in the frame arm, in the same direction for every model. The effect was largest where a model's unprompted defaults were weakest: the frame supplies the discipline a model lacks. All 500 outputs, prompts, checkers, scoring code, and the pre-registration are published with a DOI, so any team can re-derive the result without trusting the author.

title: Reply on RC2
abstract: Abstract. Mineral prospectivity mapping is a critical task in mineral exploration, effectively integrating which demands models capable of capturing both local and global geological features. While deep learning models excel in this domain, their "black-box" nature often limits the trust and insights geologists can derive from their predictions. This paper introduces a novel and interpretable hybrid model to explicitly address this challenge. Our architecture synergistically combines a deformable convolutional network for adapting spatially varying local mineralization features, such as geochemical anomalies, a Transformer module for modelling long-range global-scale spatial features governing mineral deposition. A pivotal innovation is the incorporation of an attribution branching network that generates significance scores for each input predictive factor to the final prospectivity probability. These scores not only provide a direct interpretation of factor relevance but are also fed back to dynamically modulate the key values in the Transformer's attention mechanism, effectively injecting prior geological knowledge into the local and global feature learning process. This design fosters a more geologically informed integration of local and global representations. The model's performance is evaluated against benchmark models including standalone deformable convolutional network, Transformer, and a hybrid model with deformable convolutional network and Transformer. Results demonstrate a superior predictive accuracy and more geologically plausible prospectivity maps. Furthermore, we provide a multi-faceted interpretation framework: the attribution branching network quantifies the contribution of each evidence layer, while gradient-weighted class activation mapping visualizes the discriminative local regions highlighted by the convolutional components and attention maps reveal the long-range feature relationships prioritized by the Transformer to elucidate how the model hierarchically integrates local and global features to arrive at its decisions. This dual-path interpretation strategy demystifies the model's decision-making process, offering geologists tangible insights into both "where" and "why" the model identifies high-potential zones, thereby bridging the gap between high-performing deep learning and actionable c intelligence.

Results demonstrate a superior predictive accuracy and more geologically plausible prospectivity maps. Furthermore, we provide a multi-faceted interpretation framework: the attribution branching network quantifies the contribution of each evidence layer, while gradient-weighted class activation mapping visualizes the discriminative local regions highlighted by the convolutional components and attention maps reveal the long-range feature relationships prioritized by the Transformer to elucidate how the model hierarchically integrates local and global features to arrive at its decisions. title: Time-scaled quantum simulation of dissipative nanoelectronics with zero gate overhead
abstract: Abstract Simulating open quantum systems (OQS) is essential for understanding quantum thermodynamics and materials science. However, noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices are severely bottlenecked by limited coherence times and gate infidelities. Conventional quantum simulations of Amplitude-Damping Lindblad dynamics requires active dissipative gates and ancilla environments, leading to spurious qubit flips, state saturation, and a significant two-qubit overhead. While recent methods exploit intrinsic hardware noise for quantum simulation, they mainly rely on tailored decoherence-inducing gates or complex error mitigation. Here, we introduce a hardware-intrinsic time-scaling methodology that completely eliminates active dissipative gates. By mapping the processor's continuous energy relaxation (T1) explicitly via native delay instructions, our protocol captures targeted dissipative dynamics with a strict O(1) algorithmic overhead, bypassing conventional mitigation sampling costs. We experimentally demonstrate this efficient approach on two IBM quantum architectures, successfully emulating tight-binding parameter regimes. These include nanosecond magnon propagation in yttrium iron garnet (YIG) spin chains, as well as ultrafast picosecond phonon dynamics across 1D transport channels within 2D molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) and multi-site graphene lattices. Furthermore, to mitigate error accumulation in multi-site arrays, we implement a depth-dependent scaling protocol. Finally, the proposed method is extended to the fermionic domain, emulating the femtosecond relaxation of an isolated charge carrier across 4-qubit topologies. This methodology provides a scalable pathway for robust, hardware-tailored materials simulations.

title: VISTA: Video-Injected Stylized Text-to-Animation
abstract: We present VISTA, a two-stage framework for generating stylized 3D human motion by fusing structural content from text prompts with expressive style from reference videos, without requiring jointly paired (text, video, stylized motion) triplets. A Dual-channel Autoencoder first maps motion sequences and video clips into a shared latent manifold. A masked autoregressive diffusion backbone then operates within this manifold, injecting video-derived style through a dedicated late-fusion Dual-AdaLN pathway while preserving text-conditioned content structure. A cross-batch unpaired training protocol with latent cycle consistency enables joint learning across separate semantically rich and stylistically diverse datasets. As a proof-of-concept for controllable animation synthesis, we validate VISTA on rendered motion-capture references: it achieves the highest style recognition accuracy among video-conditioned methods while preserving competitive content alignment, and its decomposed 3-way classifier-free guidance provides independent, user-controllable calibration of the content-style balance at inference time.

title: Detecting Phone-Induced Pedestrian Distraction via a Multimodal Fusion Transformer
abstract: The increasing reliance on mobile phones has made phone-induced pedestrian distraction increasingly prevalent. Activities such as texting, watching videos, and making phone calls have become significant contributors to traffic accidents. Reliable detection of pedestrian distraction is essential for autonomous vehicles, as it improves situational awareness and enables timely risk assessment, thereby supporting safe motion planning and vehicle control. We propose a multimodal fusion Transformer (MFT) for detecting phone-induced pedestrian distraction. MFT jointly extracts skeletal dynamics from body pose keypoints and visual appearance features from pedestrian images, effectively leveraging the complementary information provided by the two modalities. A cross-modal attention module is proposed to capture inter-modal dependencies through multi-head cross-attention, facilitating effective fusion of complementary information across the two modalities. Then, a temporal attention fusion module, implemented with a Transformer encoder, is employed to capture temporal dependencies. MFT is trained and evaluated on a manually annotated dataset comprising 287 pedestrian instances with 20,741 images. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MFT attains an overall accuracy of 95%, exceeding the performance of six baseline approaches by 6%.

title: Man, Machine, or Both? Reconstructing AI-Patententability under the Patents and Designs Act, 2004
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence has transform technological innovation with machine learning, and neural networks, with generative AI increasingly participating in conception, testing, optimisation, and implementation of product and processes. This development has added pressure to the patent systems designed around human inventors and technologies classifiable when the Patents and Designs Act, Cap P2 LFN, 2004 was enacted. This article interrogates the patentability of AI-related inventions within Nigeria's patent framework. It argues that AI should not constitute a legal barrier to patentability, but that, the proper inquiry should remain whether claimed subject matter satisfies the statutory requirements of novelty, inventive activity, and industrial application under section 1 of the Act, while the law separately determines human inventorship and ownership consequences under sections 2 and 3. The article draws on enacted legislations, case laws, scholarly writing and comparative study to illuminate the subject matter. The paper proposes technological-neutral reforms for reconstructing the intersection between AI patentability and the Patents and Designs Act. These reforms include: recognition of AI-assisted inventions to a define limit under the Act; clarifying the position on computer-software and implemented inventions; establishing rules for AI-assisted inventorship and disclosure; improving substantive examination capacity, and creating a coherent framework for data-intensive innovation. The paper concludes that Nigeria can use patent law not merely to accommodate AI but to stimulate domestic research, technology transfer, commercialisation, and industrial development. Keywords: artificial intelligence, AI-assisted invention, patentability, inventorship, intellectual property.

title: AViGPT: Decoupling Neural Reasoning from Parametric Memory via a Sub-Millisecond Native NVMe Hardware Bus
abstract: Autoregressive language models scale parameter counts to memorize factual data within dense neural connections. Storing encyclopedic associations inside model weights creates substantial memory footprints, high inference costs, and fixed knowledge cutoffs. AViGPT is an autoregressive transformer architecture that decouples syntactic language reasoning from factual storage. The system pairs a 183-million parameter neural core with a native hardware memory bus directly interfacing with local NVMe SSD storage. An explicit nine-token instruction set coordinates execution: the model pauses generation, queries local SQLite FTS5 storage, retrieves verified context in 1.18 milliseconds, and completes responses with verified factual precision. The architecture was pretrained on 5.0 billion tokens of English Wikipedia and FineWeb-Edu text, then aligned on 25,850 task trajectories. Empirical benchmarks confirm a 0.4 GB RAM footprint on consumer CPUs, sub-2ms storage retrieval latency, deterministic arithmetic execution, and immediate zero-shot knowledge insertion via direct disk writes without weight modification.

title: Confidence-Aware Teacher-Student Distillation for 3D Medical Segmentation
abstract: Medical image segmentation models typically rely on large amounts of densely annotated volumetric data, limiting their scalability across tasks and imaging modalities. This work addresses the challenge of predicting entire 3D anatomical structures from extreme annotation sparsity. An annotation-efficient student-teacher framework is proposed for automatic 3D medical segmentation that requires only a set of point prompts on a single 2D slice per volume, as input. A foundation model serves as an offline teacher, utilizing the provided point prompts from the selected slice to full-volume pseudo-annotations alongside their corresponding spatial confidence scores prior to student training. To mitigate the error propagation of noisy pseudo-annotations, a task-specific 3D student network is trained using a confidence-aware optimization strategy. By leveraging the teacher's pre-computed confidence scores, this strategy explicitly excludes statically uncertain regions of the pseudo-annotations from the loss calculation, while simultaneously emphasizing regions with higher confidence. Evaluated on 3D cardiac MRI datasets, our framework outperforms state-of-the-art semi-supervised methods, improving segmentation performance by up to 43.6%. Furthermore, it drastically reduces the manual annotation burden to just a few positive point prompts per volume, while improving surface boundary precision by up to 14.7% over the teacher and successfully recovering up to 34.1% of the performance gap toward the fully supervised upper bound.

title: Static classical-quantum-entanglement trade-offs: an entropic converse and single-letter characterizations
abstract: The direct static capacity region of a bipartite quantum state describes its asymptotic conversion into classical communication, quantum communication, and entanglement, with all communication directed from Alice to Bob. This paper gives a unified entropic converse for this region. The proof treats generated and consumed resources simultaneously and derives all three information inequalities for one local instrument. Its main ingredients are no-signalling, the chain rule, strong subadditivity, and continuity of conditional entropy. A supporting-hyperplane characterization leads to the static capacity formula, which is helpful in determining single-letterization of the capacity region. For a pure state of entanglement entropy $h$ subjected to erasure with probability $p$, the complete region is the convex hull of $0$ and $(0,-ph,(1-p)h)$, plus the unit-resource cone. This statement holds for arbitrary collective instruments by using subset-entropy inequalities related to earlier methods used for the dynamic capacity region of the erasure channel. Complete characterizations also hold for symmetrically extendible states and locally flagged pure-state mixtures. For maximally correlated states, the optimization over local instruments admits an exact matrix formulation and an additive outer bound. An explicit qubit example shows that a nonorthogonal discarded quantum memory can outperform every efficient instrument and every instrument with conditionally commuting discarded states. For states obtained by qubit dephasing of Schmidt-aligned pure states, an exact threshold characterizes when the static capacity formula vanishes, at every blocklength and after regularization. Full single-letter characterizations for general Hadamard states and for the remaining trade-offs for dephased states remain open, with sufficient additivity conditions identified.

title: Experimental Reproducibility Package for "Model for Improving the Quality of Uncertain Clustering"
abstract: This record contains the experimental reproducibility package accompanying the study “Model for Improving the Quality of Uncertain Clustering.” The package provides the complete Jupyter notebook, generated figures, run-level results, aggregated summaries, parameter-sensitivity analyses, bootstrap-stability estimates, drift-response measurements, and paired statistical comparisons. The experimental evaluation compares Fuzzy C-Means (FCM), Possibilistic C-Means (PCM), Possibilistic Fuzzy C-Means (PFCM), and entropy-regularized FCM across five datasets: Iris, Wine, Breast Cancer Wisconsin, Digits represented by four unsupervised principal components, and an imbalanced overlapping synthetic dataset. The methods are evaluated under baseline conditions, Gaussian measurement noise, missing values followed by median imputation, and partial mean-shift drift. The full protocol uses ten paired random seeds, three initializations per fit, and twenty bootstrap resamples for each dataset–scenario–model combination. Class labels are excluded from model fitting and hyperparameter selection and are used only for external evaluation. The archive is organised into code, figures, and results directories. The notebook contains the complete workflow required to reproduce the reported experiments.

title: AN EMPIRICAL ASSESSMENT OF THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON INDIAN PATENT AND COPYRIGHT LAW: REFORM PRIORITIES FOR GLOBAL HARMONIZATION
abstract: AI is fast changing how innovation and creative production are conceived and created, upending the traditional understanding of inventorship, authorship, and ownership as provided by intellectual property (IP) law. This study evaluates the necessity for legal reforms in Indian patent and copyright law in the wake of the advent of AI and to assess its impact on patent/copyright law from an empirical perspective. A structured questionnaire survey was carried out with legal professionals, scholars, patent agents, researchers in AI and industry practitioners to understand the perception on AI-generated inventions, ownership of such inventions, legal uncertainty, and policy preparedness. The findings show that there are many concerns related to ownership uncertainty, lack of legal provisions and growing cross-border disputes surrounding creations facilitated by AI. Comparative analysis shows that India's existing IP regime should be updated in order to be in line with the international standards. Taking into account the empirical findings, the study recommends legislative changes specific to AI, uniform guidelines on inventorship and authorship, mandatory disclosure of AI and more international harmonization. These recommendations seek to build a robust IP system in India and promote responsible innovation through the use of AI.

title: Cross-Modal Attention Driven Multi-Task Learning for Multilingual Abusive Video Classification
abstract: Multimodal learning has advanced automated abusive content detection, yet low-resource multilingual and code-mixed settings remain insufficiently explored. Existing studies provide limited modelling of cross-modal interactions, while fine-grained abusive video classification remains underexplored. To address these gaps, this work introduces AbusiveVid, a hierarchically annotated Bangla–English multimodal dataset comprising 1,680 real-world videos collected from Facebook, YouTube, and TikTok. The dataset supports both binary and fine-grained multiclass classification, with the latter encompassing Hate Speech, Offensive Language, and Threat and Violence. Cohen’s and Fleiss’ Kappa coefficients exceed 0.84, indicating high inter-annotator agree-ment. Building upon AbusiveVid, this work proposes a multi-task learning framework that integrates cross-modal attention within a shared backbone, enabling joint optimisation of both classification tasks through interactions among textual, visual, and audio representations. The framework achieves 84.53% accuracy and 83.97% Macro-F1 for binary classification, alongside 81.36% accuracy and 80.32% Macro-F1 for multiclass classification. Its robustness and generalisability are further assessed through cross-dataset evaluation, stratified five-fold cross-validation, ablation analysis, and Grad-CAM interpretation. Cross-dataset evaluation yields Macro-F1 scores of 81.10%, 97.12%, and 97.96% on MultiHateClip, ToxVidLM, and AIRTLab, respectively. Cross-validation demonstrates consistent performance across data partitions, while ablation analysis quantifies modality-specific contributions and Grad-CAM provides qualitative insights into model interpretability.

title: Iterative Atom Refinement: A Monotonicity Principle for Dictionary Learning
abstract: Dictionary learning seeks to recover an unknown dictionary $A$ from observations ${\bf y}_i = A{\bf x}_i$ with sparse coefficient vectors ${\bf x}_i$. We introduce the \emph{Iterative Atom Refinement} (IAR) algorithm, a simple procedure for recovering individual dictionary atoms. Starting from a random direction, IAR repeatedly selects the observations most strongly correlated with the current iterate and updates the direction by averaging the selected data. Our main contribution is a rigorous convergence theory of IAR. Using high-dimensional probabilistic estimates and a novel monotonicity principle for atom-selection probabilities, we show that a small initial advantage of one atom is amplified until that atom is isolated. Under our model assumptions, IAR identifies a generating atom after only three refinement steps. Numerical experiments support the theory and show that the resulting dynamics accurately capture the behavior observed in dictionary refinement.

title: Pay More Attention To Text In High-Resolution MLLMs
abstract: Failures of high-resolution MLLMs are commonly attributed to a visual problem, motivating zooming, cropping, and related visual interventions to recover fine-grained evidence or suppress interference. Yet recent studies suggest that relevant visual evidence is already encoded in intermediate representations, indicating that visual-side improvements alone insufficient. This raises a natural question: does the remaining bottleneck lie in the text that guides visual search? We identify a previously overlooked linguistic bottleneck: questions formulated for answering do not necessarily specify the visual evidence required for localization. To address this mismatch, we introduce EviSpec, a training-free compiler that derives complementary evidence specifications while preserving the original question for final reasoning. We further validate it through matched-control experiments that isolate the roles of evidence specification and localization. With the search budget fixed, structured evidence specifications yield an 8.6% relative gain over generic requests. With evidence geometry matched, the evidence localized by EviSpec yields a 14.8% relative gain over random evidence. Together, these controls isolate the benefit of specifying what evidence to seek rather than merely expanding visual access. Across all five MLLMs, EviSpec consistently improves upon the corresponding baseline on each of the three benchmarks, yielding average relative gains of \textbf{10.4%, 8.8%, and 12.4%} on V\textsuperscript{*}Bench, HR-Bench-4K, and HR-Bench-8K, respectively. Beyond high-resolution reasoning, EviSpec also achieves state-of-the-art performance on VQA and hallucination-focused benchmarks.

title: CHLOE: A Persistent Epistemic Architecture for Inspectable AI
abstract: This paper proposes a persistent epistemic architecture for AI systems in which durable cognitive state is explicit and independent of any particular language model. The persistent substrate maintains inspectable, scoped beliefs with provenance, distinguishes individual sources and accumulates domain-sensitive trust, retains unresolved questions across interactions, and supports offline consolidation that detects contradictions and generates hypotheses. Its contents participate directly in subsequent learning and action rather than serving only as retrieved memory. A dependency-free prototype instantiates this core, with language models at both linguistic interfaces, to illustrate the cycle by which attributed testimony becomes revisable belief. The central claim is that continual learning requires explicit epistemic structure: a representation of what the system believes, why it believes it, whom it learned it from, and what remains unresolved, if its evolving epistemic state is to remain inspectable and correctable. This becomes increasingly consequential as AI systems contribute to their own development, because increasing capability does not necessarily entail a corresponding improvement in epistemic reliability. Persistent epistemic state provides a substrate on which correction and calibration can accumulate over time while remaining externally auditable. Preprint submitted to arXiv in September 2026. Source code and demonstrator: https://github.com/protopopescu/chloe and https://lftm.gla.ac.uk/chloe/

title: Athena-Class Model A: Dataset and Reproducibility Artifacts
abstract: This record provides the specialized fine-tuning dataset for Athena-Class Model A and related artifacts for reproducibility. Included in this record: Athena-Class Model A training dataset New papers written by the precursor to Model A that are included in the dataset (human-assisted recursive relf-improvement) "Category 6" question results (refer to earlier Athena-class preprints) Scripts and other artifacts (fine-tune, adapter merge, quantization to Q8_0, etc.) If you intend to reproduce the Model A, it is critical that you understand the parameters included in the training script. A few key points to understand: This is not a typical configuration, particularly for a Rank 336 / Alpha 672 fine-tune (the maximum my hardware will reasonably allow) 16K max sequence length is necessary to accomodate each training segment (system prompt + data + model output) Remember to use the Gemma 4 official jinja The model's output is included in the fine-tune (no artificial prompt pairs)
