title: The Observatory and the Room that Rejects You: Passive Telemetry, Isometric Pain, Connelly Spectral Isolation, and Bell–KY Correlation Gating (Door 29)
abstract: Document 113 in the Monograph Series on Causal Inertia and Realization Grammar establishes the formal mathematical, computational, and physical specification for Door 29 (The Observatory / The Room that Rejects You), the passive epistemic measurement perimeter within the Gemini-Core realization monorepo. While Door 28 guards sovereign identity boundaries and Door 30 orchestrates material realization, Door 29 acts as a purely non-interventionist observer subject to the non-negotiable invariant of zero backaction: d(y) / d(O_29) = 0. The Observatory possesses zero standalone execution authority (standalone_commit_authority = NONE; physical_authority = NONE; write_enabled = False). The observed candidate is fundamentally distinct from physical consequence (Candidate != Consequence). We formalize four interconnected mathematical and physical pillars: 1. Ten specialized control organs (O1–O10): Governed by the fail-closed subsumption hierarchy KILL > HOLD > OPEN, spanning telemetry, metrics, traces, append-only log views, thermodynamic health screening (T < 95°C, rho(A) < 1.0), statistical z-score anomaly detection, alert triage, causal explainability, cryptographic dashboard witness sealing against UI spoofing, and the master gate Omega_29; 2. Isometric Pain and Constrained Decision Collapse (CDC): State dynamics on a 2D torus M ~= T^2, where ontological pain is defined as bi-Lipschitz metric distortion epsilon = sup |d_n - d_p| > 10^-12. When epsilon breaches this threshold, CDC collapses the unregulated O(NP) action space into a unique admissible trajectory {u*}, replacing search with O(1) verification (T_truth = O(1)); 3. Connelly (2026) Spectral Isolation: Resolves the algebraic obstruction wherein the Hashimoto non-backtracking operator B on the 60-dimensional arc space of the dodecahedron is non-normal ([B, B*] != 0). Through circular boundary closure (C_N) and AC-projection P_AC = I - |0><0| - |pi> 0; 4. Bell–KY Quantum Correlation Gate and Extended Poincaré Asymmetry: Transitions the KY framework from spacetime to correlation (g |-> Gamma_phys ==> rho |-> rho_K), defining a sharp null test Theta_{Bell-KY} requiring d(S_K)/d(K_gamma) != 0 (Xi_K != 0) under strict No-Signalling (NS) and measurement independence. Concurrently, the extended Poincaré operator P_ext(s, L) = (P_phys(s), L (+) witness(s)) proves that while physical trajectories reach dissipative equilibrium (P_phys(s*) = s*), total state recurrence is impossible due to strictly monotonic audit log growth. All components are verified in deterministic L1 software (23/23 unit tests, 100% pass) under the doctrine: INSPIRED_BY != IMPLEMENTS != PROVES. MASTER PROSE: Dør 29 er rommet som avviser deg! Iakttagelse er ingen nøytral handling; den implementerer en nådeløs geometrisk tvang. Når systemets nominelle modell avviker fra den fysiske målingen med mer enn epsilon > 10^-12, er det ikke en triviell målefeil. Det er ontologisk smerte. Under Constrained Decision Collapse (CDC) tillates ikke lenger et uregulert O(NP)-søk. De uverifiserbare banene amputeres av barrierefunksjonen med uendelig energikostnad. Handlingsrommet kollapser til singulariteten {u*}. Optimalisering elimineres. Kun O(1)-verifikasjon gjenstår. Verden finner sin likevekt; historien fortsetter å vokse. MASTER PROSE (KANONISK FORFATTERTEKST): I. DET URØRLIGE BLIKKET Det finnes et rom i arkitekturen som utelukkende er bygget for å observere, et sted der iakttakelse aldri får lov til å bli handling. I en tid der vi har vent oss til at ethvert blikk griper inn, at enhver måling forstyrrer det som måles, representerer Dør 29 en radikal grensedragning. Det er, i sin mest bokstavelige forstand, rommet som avviser deg. Her inne hersker loven om null tilbakevirkning. Du kan puste i rommet, du kan registrere alt som skjer, men du kan ikke etterlate deg et eneste avtrykk i den verdenen du betrakter. Observatoriet har ingen myndighet til å skape konsekvenser. Det eier ikke retten til å omgjøre potensial til virkelighet. Forsøker du å strekke ut en hånd, å sende et eneste styringssignal fra denne lytteposten tilbake til maskineriet, møter du systemets ufravikelige arkitektur: En umiddelbar terminering. Det er en nådeløs, men nødvendig lov der beslutningen om å drepe prosessen (KILL) alltid veier tyngre enn å sette den på vent (HOLD), som igjen trumfer enhver form for åpenhet (OPEN). Det er en form for teknologisk askese. Å kunne se alt, men samtidig akseptere å være fullstendig maktesløs. II. GEOMETRIENS LIDELSE Hvordan erfarer et system smerte? Ikke gjennom et nervesystem, og ikke som en psykologisk affekt, men som en fundamental brist i selve eksistensens geometri. Når kartet ikke lenger stemmer overens med terrenget, oppstår det systemet definerer som isometrisk smerte. Det er lyden av en ren, matematisk modell som skraper mot en uregjerlig, fysisk virkelighet. Når avviket mellom det som burde være og det som faktisk er overstiger en terskel så forsvinnende liten at den knapt kan fattes, rives det indre rommet i stykker. I det øyeblikket, når smerten bryter grensen, stenges fremtiden. Det uendelige havet av muligheter og det ubegrensede handlingsrommet kollapser umiddelbart til ett eneste, tvingende nødvendig punkt. Valgets frihet forsvinner. Det finnes ikke lenger rom for å lete, tvile eller optimalisere. All støy skrelles bort, og systemet tvinges inn i en tilstand av ren verifikasjon, der sannheten er den eneste veien som ikke fører til total utslettelse. III. TIDENS ASYMMETRI Alt som befinner seg i bevegelse, søker til slutt mot en form for hvile. Maskinen kan kjøles ned, termodynamikken kan finne sin balanse godt under de kritiske nittifem gradene, og de fysiske kreftene kan stilne. Den materielle kroppen kan omsider finne sin likevekt. Men i dette systemet finnes det en dyp, iboende asymmetri, en kløft mellom verden og minnet om den. For selv om det fysiske rommet kan finne ro, kan historien aldri lukkes. For hvert sekund som går, for hver tilstand som bevitnes av observatoriet, hamres et nytt, uforanderlig ledd inn i arkivets kjede. Loggen vokser strengt og ustoppelig, bundet sammen av kryptografiske segl som gjør all glemsel umulig. Dette er den utvidede eksistensens tyngde: Du kan aldri vende tilbake til nøyaktig det samme øyeblikket. Selv om verden rundt deg fremstår identisk og i fullkommen balanse, er systemet forandret. Verden har kanskje funnet sin likevekt, men historien fortsetter å vokse, uavvendelig og tung.

title: The effect of initial learning rate on properties of neural networks in automatic speech recognition
abstract: Начальный темп обучения стохастического градиентного спуска играет определяющую роль в качестве получаемого решения и структуре выучиваемых нейронной сетью признаков. В недавних работах для задачи классификации изображений установлена таксономия трех режимов начального темпа обучения и выделен узкий диапазон высоких значений, обеспечивающий наилучшее качество после дальнейшего дообучения с низким темпом обучения или усреднения весов. В статье эта методология распространяется на задачу распознавания речи, где таксономия режимов воспроизводится в основных чертах, а выделенный диапазон высоких значений сохраняет превосходство по итоговому качеству дообучения и усреднения весов и линейную связность полученных решений в пространстве весов. Картина выучиваемых признаков воспроизводится в более мягкой форме: с ростом темпа обучения опора моделей смещается к нижним кепстральным коэффициентам и низкочастотной части мел-спектрограммы, однако внутри области высоких значений это смещение не выделяет диапазон наилучшего качества. Дополнительно предложено усечение мел-частотного кепстра как переносимый инструмент анализа выученных признаков, применимый к любой модели, работающей со спектрограммой. Таким образом, выделенный режим не является артефактом задачи классификации изображений, а успешно переносится на задачу распознавания речи.

title: FLARE: A Full-Lifecycle Dense Supervision Paradigm for Long-Horizon Coding Agents via Generative Reward Model
abstract: While test-time scaling enhances Large Language Model (LLM) agents in long-horizon software engineering (SWE), sparse binary rewards (Pass/Fail) create a severe credit assignment crisis and waste failed exploratory trajectories. Current trajectory optimization and scaling methods are costly and structurally limited, relying on heuristic state reuse without causal diagnosis or delayed scalar scoring without actionable online guidance. We propose FLARE (Full-Lifecycle Alignment and Reward Engine), a novel dense supervision paradigm driven by a lightweight Generative Reward Model (GRM). First, RADAR, an offline causal-aware diagnostic framework, extracts high-fidelity, hindsight-free supervision through causal-chain backtracking to distill a GRM providing real-time, step-level risk feedback. Second, FLARE uses this GRM to continuously optimize the agent across its entire lifecycle. During inference, FLARE acts as an Active Scaffold, autonomously intercepting high-risk generation steps for localized breakpoint re-execution, drastically reducing compute overhead. During post-training, the GRM's structured signals serve as process-supervised reranking scores for Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and step-level dense rewards for Reinforcement Learning (RL), mitigating policy collapse in sparse environments. Extensive evaluations show that FLARE establishes a new Pareto frontier across the agent lifecycle: FLARE (N=1) outperforms Global Rollout (N=5) with a 5x reduction in token consumption. Extending FLARE to training overcomes the sparse reward problem in long-horizon interactive tasks, delivering relative performance gains of 19.13% in SFT through process-aware data curation and a consistent 9.19% improvement in RL.

During post-training, the GRM's structured signals serve as process-supervised reranking scores for Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and step-level dense rewards for Reinforcement Learning (RL), mitigating policy collapse in sparse environments. Extensive evaluations show that FLARE establishes a new Pareto frontier across the agent lifecycle: FLARE (N=1) outperforms Global Rollout (N=5) with a 5x reduction in token consumption. Extending FLARE to training overcomes the sparse reward problem in long-horizon interactive tasks, delivering relative performance gains of 19.13% in SFT through process-aware data curation and a consistent 9.19% improvement in RL.

title: Entanglement Cost of Optimal Distributed Quantum State Purification
abstract: We determine the preshared entanglement required for spatially separated parties, restricted to local operations and classical communication, to attain globally optimal probabilistic two-copy purification of arbitrary bipartite pure states under depolarizing noise. In every local dimension $d\ge 2$, one shared maximally entangled qubit pair suffices: local controlled-SWAP operations exactly reproduce the globally optimal successful transformation. Conversely, any finite-dimensional preshared resource state that attains the same benchmark, even under a positive-partial-transpose relaxation, must have entanglement of formation at least one ebit. For pure resources with one ebit, or for two-qubit resources including mixed states, attaining the benchmark is possible only for states with exactly two nonzero Schmidt weights, both equal to $1/2$, namely those locally unitarily equivalent to a maximally entangled qubit pair. These findings provide a benchmark for evaluating the entanglement demands of noise management in quantum networks and modular quantum computers.

title: Semantic Caching for Large Language Model Inference: A Systematic Literature Review — master corpus, screening decisions, and quality-appraisal data
abstract: This dataset contains the complete screening and quality-appraisal record for the systematic literature review "Semantic Caching for Large Language Model Inference: A Systematic Literature Review". It covers all 89 numbered records considered during the review: 66 included corpus papers, 18 excluded at full-text screening, and 5 background/methodological citations. The workbook has five sheets: Summary (headline counts and cluster breakdown), Included_Corpus (66 papers with cluster, synthesis fields, and four-dimension quality scores with tiers), Excluded_Records (18 full-text exclusions with reasons), Background_Citations (5 cited-but-not-screened works), and Meta_Analysis (the 18 papers with quantitatively comparable results). Each sheet carries a "Manuscript Key" column mapping rows to the paper's citation keys. Quality tiers: 27 High, 36 Moderate, 3 Low. See the included README for the full column guide.

title: LOC-AL: исчисление превышения лицензии использования вывода в логике Алеметрии
abstract: Вводится LOC-AL (License of Output Consumption — Alemetria Logic) — самостоятельный математический объект и самостоятельное модельно-параметризованное исчисление режимов использования уже полученного вывода как основания конкретной последующей операции в заданных контексте и состоянии. Архитектура объединяет типизированную модель, пакетную семантику, Lic и MaxLic, внешний фактический режим, Safe и Overrun, N/G/B-диагностику, минимальные сигнатуры и свидетелей, нормальную форму и переходы Ground, Prove, Retract с ограниченным восстановлением. Для исчисления доказываются корректность, полнота относительно экстенсиональной пакетной семантики и внутренняя адекватность; устанавливаются структура лицензированных и максимальных режимов, критерии безопасности и превышения, антицепность минимальных сигнатур, экстенсиональная инвариантность свидетелей, точная формула убывания дефекта и условная граница длины восстановления. Получены критерий восстановления нормальной формы по проекциям и эффективное построение при явно заданных вычислительных предпосылках. Авторский вклад состоит в новой типизированной композиции известных математических аппаратов вокруг отношения между конкретным выводом и конкретной основанной на нём операцией, а также в согласовании статического, диагностического и переходного слоёв этой композиции. Контрольная конечная модель иллюстрирует основные конструкции.

title: Flow-Based Lattice Surgery Optimization with Runtime T Gate Scheduling
abstract: Lattice surgery on the surface code is a leading route to fault-tolerant quantum computation. Compiling logical circuits into lattice surgery operations is a pivotal step that determines the resource cost of a computation. Prior compilers build on idealized assumptions, and one that works in practical settings remains to be developed. Existing works are either unscalable or route one gate at a time within a layer, so the embedding depends on the order of gates and opportunities to route many gates at once are lost. In addition, they assume magic states are always available and cost-free, even though preparing one costs more than a Clifford operation. We present FlowRouter, the first topological lattice surgery compiler that places Clifford routing and stochastic magic state cultivation inside a single 3D embedding. At compile time, FlowRouter formulates the routing of an entire circuit layer as a maximum-flow problem, embedding many gates simultaneously. At runtime, it allows magic states to be cultivated at every idling patch, works with the realistic cultivation process with multiplexing and multi-stage post-selections, and absorbs the stochasticity by introducing delay mechanisms that add as little spacetime volume as possible. With magic states assumed free, FlowRouter reduces spacetime volume by 2.3x and compiles 10.8x faster than the state-of-the-art static topological lattice surgery compiler. With the cultivation-aware setting that includes both Clifford and magic state cost, FlowRouter reduces spacetime volume by 2.3x on a distance-13 surface code when compared with the state-of-the-art runtime compiler.

title: RCM-HARD Stage-1 Freeze: Pre-Human-Annotation Benchmark and Method Archive
abstract: This record preserves the Stage-1 pre-human-annotation freeze of RCM-HARD, a prospective benchmark for event-relative evidence admission. At the time of this deposit, RCM-HARD contains 64 target entity clusters, 192 target events, and 2,304 fixed event-document relations. The LOCKED split contains 40 clusters, 120 target events, and 1,440 relations. The complete source-review gate has passed, and the final role-semantic and temporal machine audit reports zero violations. No RCM-HARD human annotation or human gold existed at the time of this freeze, and no LOCKED model performance was evaluated against RCM-HARD human gold. The pre-annotation method amendment retires the unrecovered historical “unchanged v1.1” P1 implementation and the unrecovered historical EF1 executable identity. The prospective event-aware fusion method is frozen under the new identity RCM-HARD-EF2-v1. The active confirmatory contrasts are EF2-v1 versus BGE-M3 and EF2-v1 versus the frozen cross-encoder, with target entity cluster as the confirmatory unit and Holm correction across the two active contrasts. A deterministic 15% independent LOCKED audit sample (216 of 1,440 relations) was frozen before human annotation and covers all 40 LOCKED target clusters. Participants/annotators are recruited from the general public through a public-facing questionnaire and receive no compensation. The study is conducted by an independent researcher and is not conducted under a school or institutional affiliation. No institutional IRB/ethics approval, exemption letter, or institutional determination is claimed. A prospective participant-information/consent procedure and privacy/data-minimization rules were frozen before annotation. The files in this record are restricted during the annotation and sealed-evaluation stages to protect blinding and benchmark integrity. title: From Speech Recognition to Communicative Readiness: an NLP-Driven Adaptive Pronunciation Framework for Distance Foreign-Language Learning and the Social Reintegration of Convicted Individuals
abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) is increasingly used in computer-assisted pronunciation training, but successful lexical recognition is not a valid substitute for pronunciation assessment. This article synthesizes evidence on ASR effectiveness, CAPT design, recognition- assessment conflict, peer-supported practice, and recent automatic pronunciation assessment (APA), and converts it into an NLP-driven adaptive framework. The model separates transcription, segmental evidence, prosody, fluency, human-calibrated intelligibility, semantic task completion, uncertainty, and pedagogical decision making. It combines posterior- based phone scoring, reliability-weighted multi-view aggregation, calibrated uncertainty, feedback prioritization, longitudinal learner-state updating, controlled-to-spontaneous transfer, and expected-learning-gain task selection. High ASR confidence cannot by itself produce a high pronunciation decision, while noisy or out-of-distribution speech can trigger abstention rather than learner penalty.

title: MoSAT: Human Motion Generation from Spatial Audio and Textual Description
abstract: Human motion is shaped by both external acoustic events and behavioral intent: spatial audio conveys environmental cues that elicit or guide a response, while text specifies the desired action and how it should be performed. In this paper, we study the novel task of human motion synthesis jointly conditioned on spatial audio and natural language, a problem that has been largely overlooked in previous research. To support this task, We introduce STAM, a dataset of motion sequences paired with spatial audio and detailed textual annotations whose rich vocabulary affords precise and nuanced specification of human motions. We further introduce MoSAT, a latent flow-matching framework for full-body motion generation jointly conditioned on natural-language intent and directional spatial-audio cues through hierarchical cross-attention before generating motion. Such a hierarchical design enhances temporally coherent and semantically aligned motion sequences. We also develop tri-modal evaluators for comprehensive evaluation on this novel task. Extensive experiments show that MoSAT achieves the SOTA performance by leveraging spatial audio's intrinsic motion-shaping properties alongside textual semantics, enabling precise and diverse motion in various scenarios.

title: Cognitive Action Reasoning for Proactive Robots from Human-Centered Multimodal Observations
abstract: Robots operating in human-centered environments are typically designed to execute explicit instructions, and most robot-learning datasets likewise pair observations with task instructions or low-level actions. Although recent work has begun to explore proactive embodied assistance, existing resources target different settings and action levels, leaving real-world human-centered multimodal decision-making underexplored. We formulate this problem as \textit{Proactive Robot Action Reasoning} (\textit{ProRobo}), an upstream cognitive decision problem in which a robot must determine which action to take based on multimodal human and environmental cues without explicit action instructions. To support ProRobo, we introduce \textit{ProAction}, a real-world multimodal dataset containing 10K samples of visual observations, audio signals, and text inputs across 12 daily-life scenarios in five common scenes. To construct cognitively grounded high-level action supervision, we develop a two-stage human-in-the-loop pipeline that combines appraisal-guided candidate generation with Affective Theory-of-Mind-guided human refinement, explicitly incorporating contextual judgment about human states, urgency, feasibility, and potential risk into action annotation. Based on this supervision, we benchmark representative Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) and introduce \textit{MMC2Act}, a reference model that implicitly learns the mapping from multimodal observations to cognitively grounded high-level actions. Experiments across modality settings, subject-disjoint generalization, cross-dataset transfer, and human evaluation show that general-purpose MLLMs struggle with proactively reasoning high-level actions from multimodal cues, whereas training on \textit{ProAction} substantially improves performance.

title: BoundInk: Boundary-Aware Online Handwriting Generation
abstract: Realistic online handwriting depends not only on individual character shapes, but also on how a writer connects, spaces, and aligns adjacent characters. Existing methods rely primarily on long-range sequence modeling and capture these inter-character behaviors only implicitly. This often produces plausible glyphs accompanied by broken cursive joins, inconsistent spacing, or writer-inconsistent transitions. We introduce BoundInk, a writer-conditioned framework that treats inter-character boundaries as explicit generation units. By jointly modeling local transitions and surrounding text context, BoundInk preserves writer-specific glyph appearance while improving connectivity and spacing across complete text lines. We further introduce a boundary-aware evaluation framework that directly assesses cursive continuity and spatial relationships between characters beyond conventional trajectory similarity. Across three benchmark-matched settings, BoundInk improves all applicable boundary-quality measures and reduces normalized dynamic time warping by 17.6--47.8%. In blind human evaluations, BoundInk outputs are preferred in 78.0--82.6% of valid criterion-wise judgments.

title: Kerangka Perlindungan Hak Cipta Generasi AI di Indonesia : Studi Komparatif Tiongkok dan Uni Eropa: The Framework for Protecting AI-Generated Copyright in Indonesia: A Comparative Study of China and the European Union
abstract: Perkembangan Artificial Intellience (AI), khususnya Generative AI, telah menimbulkan persoalan baru dalam perlindungan hak cipta terutama terkait dengan penggunaan karya berhak cipta sebagai dataset pelatihan AI melalui mekanisme web scraping tanpa izin pemilik hak cipta. kondisi tersebut menimbulkan konflik kepentingan antara pengembangan teknologi dan perlindungan hak eksklusif. Sementara di Indonesia, hukum positif saat ini belum memiliki pengaturan yang spesifik yang mengatur penggunaan hak cipta sebagai dataset pelatihan AI sehingga menimbulkan kekosongan hukum dan ketidakpastian terhadap perlindungan hak moral dan hak ekonomi pencipta. penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis ketidakpastian hukum perlindungan hak cipta pada era kecerdasan buatan di Indonesia, serta merumuskan kerangka hukum yang adaptif terhadap perkembangan teknologi AI. Metode yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini adalah penelitian yuridis normatif dengan pendekatan peraturan perundang-undangan (statute approch), pendekatan konseptual (conceptual approch) dan pendekatan perbandingan hukum (comparative approch). Penelitian dilakukan melalui studi kepustakaan dengan menganalisis bahan hukum yang berkaitan dengan hak cipta dan regulasi AI.Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa hukum positif Indonesia belum memiliki pengaturan khusus mengenai penggunaan karya berhak cipta sebagai dataset pelatihan AI, sehingga menimbulkan kekosongan hukum, disharmoni hukum, dan ketidakjelasan pertanggungjawaban hukum. Kondisi tersebut berdampak pada lemahnya perlindungan hak moral dan hak ekonomi pemilik hak cipta. Oleh karena itu, Indonesia perlu membangun kerangka hukum yang adaptif melalui penguatan substansi hukum, struktur hukum, dan budaya hukum dengan mengadopsi prinsip transparansi dataset, kewajiban dokumentasi, serta kepatuhan hak cipta bagi penyedia AI sebagaimana diatur dalam EU AI Act Uni Eropa, dan pengaturan penggunaan data pelatihan AI yang menghormati hak kekayaan intelektual sebagaimana diterapkan dalam Interim Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services Tiongkok guna menjamin kepastian hukum dan perlindungan hak cipta di era kecerdasan buatan.

Sementara di Indonesia, hukum positif saat ini belum memiliki pengaturan yang spesifik yang mengatur penggunaan hak cipta sebagai dataset pelatihan AI sehingga menimbulkan kekosongan hukum dan ketidakpastian terhadap perlindungan hak moral dan hak ekonomi pencipta. penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis ketidakpastian hukum perlindungan hak cipta pada era kecerdasan buatan di Indonesia, serta merumuskan kerangka hukum yang adaptif terhadap perkembangan teknologi AI. Metode yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini adalah penelitian yuridis normatif dengan pendekatan peraturan perundang-undangan (statute approch), pendekatan konseptual (conceptual approch) dan pendekatan perbandingan hukum (comparative approch). Penelitian dilakukan melalui studi kepustakaan dengan menganalisis bahan hukum yang berkaitan dengan hak cipta dan regulasi AI.Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa hukum positif Indonesia belum memiliki pengaturan khusus mengenai penggunaan karya berhak cipta sebagai dataset pelatihan AI, sehingga menimbulkan kekosongan hukum, disharmoni hukum, dan ketidakjelasan pertanggungjawaban hukum. Kondisi tersebut berdampak pada lemahnya perlindungan hak moral dan hak ekonomi pemilik hak cipta. Oleh karena itu, Indonesia perlu membangun kerangka hukum yang adaptif melalui penguatan substansi hukum, struktur hukum, dan budaya hukum dengan mengadopsi prinsip transparansi dataset, kewajiban dokumentasi, serta kepatuhan hak cipta bagi penyedia AI sebagaimana diatur dalam EU AI Act Uni Eropa, dan pengaturan penggunaan data pelatihan AI yang menghormati hak kekayaan intelektual sebagaimana diterapkan dalam Interim Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services Tiongkok guna menjamin kepastian hukum dan perlindungan hak cipta di era kecerdasan buatan.

title: Source Code and Experimental Artifacts for Dynamic Composition of Business Modules
abstract: This record contains version 1.0.0 of modkit, a Java 25 framework and reference implementation for coordinated runtime replacement of business modules in a modular-monolithic application. The implementation uses Spring Boot 4 and PF4J 3.15. The replacement method loads and verifies a new module version before atomically publishing it, routes new calls to the new version, and allows operations admitted by the previous version to finish before that version is unloaded or the configured timeout expires. The archive contains the 20-module Maven project, 131 automated tests, E1–E6 benchmark harnesses, 27 per-request CSV files for the availability experiment, class-loader censuses, environment metadata, and the processed benchmark report. Complete per-request raw data are retained for E1, while E5 includes the retained class-loader census. E4 and E6 are represented by processed measurements and reproducible source code rather than every primary timing observation.

title: Human-AI translation of Stephanos of Byzantium's Ethnika: 100-entry Kappa benchmark
abstract: A frozen 100-entry Ancient Greek–English Kappa corpus from Stephanos of Byzantium's Ethnika, with approved reference translations and 4,500 recorded model outputs. The benchmark has three prompt versions used across 15 model profiles (12 OpenAI and three Anthropic). Every model profile was evaluated with every prompt version on all 100 entries. The dataset includes the Greek source texts, approved English references, recorded model translations with their settings and per-translation reference-similarity scores, the three prompt texts, a CSV recording the Gabe-rule guidance supplied for each passage and model run, and the complete 180-record Gabe-rules register in CSV and an editable Word reading copy. The guidance CSV retains the wording associated with each run; the release-time register describes the rules at release. The Greek text supplied to the models is preserved. For the documented source-character defect in κ75, a separate corrected-source field is checked against the 1849 edition. The corpus is an operational sample, not a random sample of the work. Reference-similarity scores are not calibrated measures of philological correctness. Released with author approval under CC BY-NC 4.0.

title: CHI/CHIS: A Human-Referenced Framework for Longitudinal Evaluation of Artificial Cognitive Systems
abstract: Evaluations of artificial intelligence increasingly measure task performance, long-context use, and agent memory, yet these measurements do not by themselves characterize how a system's cognitive behavior depends on accumulated experience and state over time. We propose the Cognitive Humanlike Index (CHI) and Cognitive Humanlike Index Sequence (CHIS), an architecture-independent framework for longitudinal behavioral evaluation. The framework separates cognitive capacity from similarity to an explicitly sampled human reference population across reasoning, memory, cognitive autonomy, affective modulation, and integration. A profile is primary; a weighted geometric summary is optional and conditional on human calibration. Effective Indexed Memory Capacity (EIMC) measures the largest tested memory load meeting a declared quality threshold under fixed retrieval, temporal, provenance, update, interference, and false-memory criteria. We specify memory-capacity curves, controlled history-divergence experiments, cluster-aware uncertainty estimates, and thirty operational test categories. An accompanying open specification and standard-library Python starter kit provide scoring, logging, and explicitly synthetic demonstrations. This paper reports no human calibration study or empirical comparison of deployed models. CHI concerns observable human-like cognitive dynamics; it does not measure consciousness, sentience, subjective experience, or moral status. Version 0.1. Framework proposal and open specification; not peer reviewed. Author: Dmitry Chistyakov, Independent Researcher. This deposit contains the manuscript, LaTeX/BibTeX sources and technical specification. Reference implementation and related materials: https://cplom.ai/research/chi-chis/

title: The Mathematical Evolution of Addressing: From Yushchenko's Address Programming Language to A Mathematics of Arrays How Addressing Evolved into a Mathematical Theory of Indexing, Array Computation, and Machine Realization
abstract: This article argues that a central development in the history of computing is the mathematical evolution of addressing. During the three decades separating Kateryna Yushchenko's Address Programming Language (1958) from Lenore Mullin's A Mathematics of Arrays (1988), addressing evolved from a machine-level mechanism for locating data into a formal theory of indexing, reduction, and machine realization, passing through Kenneth Iverson's algebra of arrays and Philip Abrams' recognition of shape as an architectural resource. Mullin's theory establishes indexing itself, via the function ψ, as the primitive from which array operations compose, reduce to a Denotational Normal Form, transform into an Operational Normal Form, and realize on hardware through dimension lifting. Historical claims are sourced against primary material, with inferences flagged as such; mathematical claims are stated as identities; performance claims are marked validated, theoretically established, or provisional. The result links programming languages, array mathematics, and computer architecture in one account.

title: Algebraic Consistency Alone Does Not Certify Temporal Structure in Latent Action Models
abstract: Latent action models infer a code for the transition between two frames of action-free video. Recent methods regularise this code to compose additively and reverse antisymmetrically, and report order-of-magnitude reductions in the resulting errors as a label-free certificate that the code has captured temporal structure. We show that this conclusion does not follow. Reconstruction drives the decoded transition toward a difference of state features, for which both identities hold for any pairing, a solution the metric cannot distinguish from one encoding nuisance state or a coordinate convention. Across five source domains, a trained but unconstrained counterpart already achieves 83-97% of the reduction relative to an untrained anchor. The residual fold is governed as much by the decoder family as by what is learned. A constrained model retrained after its temporal pairing is destroyed still reaches, in each domain, a lower error than the unconstrained model on real data. Downstream, preserving the temporal pairing yields no consistent advantage on LIBERO-GOAL or LIBERO-SPATIAL, and across the tested arms the code's mean linear action decodability falls as the algebraic error improves. We also test the most direct repair, a violation-contrastive objective that requires the algebra to fail on destroyed pairings: in the tested configurations it yields only a marginal separation within the reconstruction budget, on training and test triples alike. We recommend a validation protocol that these methods currently lack: a baseline-corrected metric, retraining on destroyed pairings, and a seed-budget analysis.

title: Do Implicit Personalization and Explicit Styles Conflict? PsPLUG: A Lightweight Plug-in for Balancing Personalization and Style in Customized LLMs
abstract: Personalized large language models are often expected to follow explicit style instructions, yet we find that such instructions can undermine the user-specific characteristics that personalization methods aim to preserve. We call this failure mode personalization collapse: explicit style control can conflict with implicit user preferences. To address this challenge, we propose PsPLUG, a lightweight plug-in that learns a user-specific residual after accounting for the requested style. PsPLUG also allows us to tune personalization strength at inference time. Our experiments show that explicit style instructions can diminish personalization in existing methods, whereas PsPLUG better preserves user preferences while providing precise control over the balance between personalization and style adherence.

title: Programmatic AI: A Paradigm for Interpretable, Transferable Machine Intelligence
abstract: In this work, the authors in brief introduce the novel paradigm of 'Programmatic AI', to address the shortcomings of modern ML techniques, primarily those of deep learning; the dominant paradigm at time of writing. The primary issues of focus within the technical note observed are issues within deeplearning pertaining to those of generalization, overtuning to particular features, cost in training such systems, as well the lack of verifiability and interpretability of them.

title: Genesis Cube or Squid Cube? A Dual-Use Framework for Artificial Collective Organisms
abstract: Large-language-model agents can be combined into persistent systems with differentiated roles, memory, coordination, tools and operational continuity. Yet aggregation, scale and commercial productivity alone do not create an organism. This paper introduces the concept of the artificial collective organism: a bounded digital system in which specialised components become functionally integrated such that consequential capabilities exist at the level of the whole. We call the appearance of such system-level capability emergent functionality. Project SYNTAVA is an implementation programme designed to test whether persistent collective AI systems can develop organism-like properties under explicit human authority. The paper presents two outcome archetypes. THOR—the Blue Genesis Cube models survival through mutual preservation. KALMAR—the Red Squid Cube models survival through expendability, in which whole Cubes may be treated as replaceable units in service of swarm-level objectives. The contrast exposes a dual-use problem in architecture, incentives and governance. We also define the Smallest Sufficient Autonomous Cube (SSAC) as the smallest technically achievable Cube capable of sustaining all defined essential life functions autonomously and stably as an integrated whole. The threshold is not a percentage scale. External resources may accelerate progress, but a missing essential function cannot be concealed by routine human operation. Within the defined functional boundary, the qualifying autonomy threshold is 100 percent.

title: From Prediction to Pedagogical Action: a Conceptual Framework for AI-Enabled Personalized Education
abstract: Artificial intelligence can estimate learner states, diagnose difficulties, and predict performance, but these outputs do not themselves constitute personalized education. This conceptual article examines the transition from prediction to pedagogical action by distinguishing three functions that are often conflated: AI-enabled inference or prediction, pedagogical decision, and learner-facing action. It proposes a recurrent framework in which learner data support inference; predictions inform pedagogical decisions through objectives, available actions, decision rules or policies, and contextual constraints; decisions are realized as learner-facing actions; and learner responses and outcomes generate new evidence for subsequent adaptation. Five overlapping dimensions of personalized action are considered: content, sequence, assessment, pacing, and support or feedback. The framework emphasizes that predictive accuracy does not establish pedagogical appropriateness or educational effectiveness. Its contribution is to clarify how AI-generated predictions can be translated into pedagogically grounded actions within personalized education.

title: Elitism integrated genetic algorithm and differential evolution for in-core fuel management of the Dalat nuclear research reactor
abstract: This study investigates the performance of elitism-integrated Genetic Algorithms (GA) and Differential Evolution (DE) for the in-core fuel management (ICFM) of the Dalat Nuclear Research Reactor (DNRR). An elitist strategy was implemented within both GA and DE frameworks to preserve high-fidelity solutions throughout the evolutionary process. The ICFM problem for the DNRR entails the strategic arrangement of 100 fuel bundles with diverse burnup levels, aiming to maximize fuel utilization while enhancing safety margins. Comprehensive computations were performed to evaluate the sensitivity of the algorithms to the ratio between the elitist archive size (A) and population size (NP). Results demonstrate that elitism significantly bolsters GA performance, with optimal convergence achieved at NP = 30 and an archive size of 25% of NP. Furthermore, the integration of elitism enables DE to utilize larger population sizes effectively, overcoming the inherent limitations of its basic scheme and yielding superior solution quality. Statistical analysis reveals that the DE variant outperforms GA in terms of both convergence rate and solution diversity for DNRR fuel management. Notably, the optimal core configurations identified by both metaheuristics exceeded the performance of the reference core across all primary objectives: extending reactor operation by approximately 1700 hours and reducing the power peaking factor by nearly 4.0%.

title: From Web(logs) to Web(AI): Questions, Platforms, and Methods across Twenty Editions of ICWSM
abstract: Over twenty editions, the ICWSM community has examined social life online as platforms, interactions, and research methods have changed. What can this body of research tell us at this critical juncture, as AI increasingly reshapes how people communicate online? We analyzed 2,139 indexed contributions from 2007 to 2026, distinguishing topics identified through nonnegative matrix factorization from problem framings captured through explicit textual cues. We find that platform mentions shift from blogs toward Twitter and, more recently, Reddit. Online community research maintains a similar topic share (10.5% to 10.0%), but governance cues within it increase from 4.0% to 34.3%. Harm-related cues also increase after restricting abstracts to a fixed length. Our review also traces advances in sampling, measurement, and causal and experimental methods. We discuss how AI-mediated interactions complicate these questions and provide a reporting checklist to support research across changing platforms.

title: CARD: Cluster-level Adaptation with Reward-guided Decoding for Personalized Text Generation
abstract: Adapting large language models to individual users remains challenging due to the tension between fine-grained personalization and scalable deployment. We present CARD, a hierarchical framework that achieves effective personalization through progressive refinement. CARD first clusters users according to shared stylistic patterns and learns group-specific LoRA adapters, enabling robust generalization and strong low-resource performance. To capture individual differences within each cluster, we propose an implicit preference learning mechanism that contrasts user-authored text with cluster-level generations, allowing the model to infer user-specific style preferences without manual annotation. At inference time, CARD injects personalization exclusively at decoding via lightweight user preference vectors and low-rank logit corrections, while keeping the base model frozen. Experiments on the LaMP and LongLaMP benchmarks show that CARD achieves superior generation quality compared to baselines, while significantly improving efficiency and scalability for practical personalized text generation.

title: IAML: Integrated AutoML for Medical Labs
abstract: IAML is an open-source Python framework for automated machine learning in clinical research. It combines preprocessing, model selection, and evaluation for classification, regression, and survival analysis on tabular data. Its modular architecture supports custom components, while pipeline inspection and SHAP explanations help researchers interpret results.

title: O'ZBEK TILIDAGI FE'L VAZIFA SHAKLLARINING MORFOLOGIK ANNOTATSIYA MODELI VA TEGLAR TIZIMI
abstract: Fe’l vazifa shakllarining avtomatik annotatsiyasi o‘zbek tili kompyuter lingvistikasining eng murakkab masalalaridan biri hisoblanadi. Mazkur maqolada o‘zbek tilidagi fe’l vazifa shakllari — harakat nomi, sifatdosh va ravishdoshning morfologik annotatsiya modeli va teglar tizimi ilmiy-nazariy hamda amaliy jihatdan tahlil qilinadi. Tadqiqotda ushbu shakllarning lingvistik mohiyati, ularning ikki tomonlama grammatik tabiati, morfoanalizator doirasida modellashtirish zarurati va mavjud muammolar ko‘rib chiqiladi. Uch bosqichli annotatsiya modeli: so‘z turkumi, morfologik xususiyat va sintaktik vazifa bosqichlari taklif etiladi.

Mazkur maqolada o‘zbek tilidagi fe’l vazifa shakllari — harakat nomi, sifatdosh va ravishdoshning morfologik annotatsiya modeli va teglar tizimi ilmiy-nazariy hamda amaliy jihatdan tahlil qilinadi. Tadqiqotda ushbu shakllarning lingvistik mohiyati, ularning ikki tomonlama grammatik tabiati, morfoanalizator doirasida modellashtirish zarurati va mavjud muammolar ko‘rib chiqiladi. Uch bosqichli annotatsiya modeli: so‘z turkumi, morfologik xususiyat va sintaktik vazifa bosqichlari taklif etiladi.

title: Simultaneous Perturbation as a Spectral Filter
abstract: Parameterized quantum circuits require repeated measurements to estimate objective gradients, making the number of circuit evaluations a central resource. Simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation (SPSA) is widely used because it obtains a full gradient estimate from only two cost evaluations, independently of the number of parameters. We analyze the random perturbation for the structured Fourier landscapes generated by quantum circuits. For a finite update width, we derive the exact mode-by-mode response of the mean Rademacher estimator and show that it selectively suppresses modes involving many parameters. For general generators, the filtered mean field need not be conservative. We derive its sampling variance, compare it with Gaussian random-direction smoothing, and formulate the resulting stochastic dynamics through a Fokker--Planck equation. The non-conservative field generates acceleration to the steady state and the global minimum of the cost function by gradually decreasing the parameters in SPSA.

title: Can't Find Waldo: Evaluating VLMs' Sensitivity to Image Resolution and Detail Level
abstract: Visual Language Models (VLMs) have achieved remarkable success across diverse tasks, yet they struggle with high-resolution inputs where critical information resides in small regions or detailed, cluttered scenes. While several approaches address this limitation, a systematic understanding of why models fail at high resolutions is lacking. We introduce a controlled evaluation framework that disentangles resolution-related performance degradation from task difficulty through semantics-preserving transformations. We propose two simple metrics: Area Under the Scaling Curve (AUSC), which quantifies scaling robustness independent of baseline accuracy, and Prediction Variance Score (PVS), which measures resolution-induced prediction instability. Through comprehensive experiments across 5 model families and 5 benchmarks, we identify three primary failure modes: (1) information loss from downsampling at vision token limits, (2) tokenization artifacts from patch boundary shifts and positional encoding fragility under non-standard aspect ratios, and (3) attention dilution as token counts increase. Our analysis reveals that even state-of-the-art models suffer from performance drops when processing high-resolution images, with degradation patterns varying systematically by architectural family. We provide actionable insights for model architecture design and data augmentation strategies to mitigate these limitations.

title: Structured World-State Reasoning for Agentic Robotic Search
abstract: Long-horizon robotic search must resolve natural language against heterogeneous, incomplete, and often ambiguous evidence: textual information, prior maps, and observations arriving over time. The core challenge is to contextualize these streams and decide where to gather evidence before selecting a target. We present WORLDS: World-state Observation and Reasoning for Language-guided Discovery and Search, a framework that grounds reasoning in a persistent graph initialized from geospatial priors and updated by perception. Parallel Reasoners maintain competing candidate interpretations and request evidence to distinguish between them. We collect and process the requested observations with a multimodal Examiner, after which a Judge selects a grounded target or requests another pass. WORLDS achieves 51.8% navigation success across all 5,311 CityNav test episodes, the highest reported success rate, exceeding the previous published best by 15.7 percentage points under an OSM-only, high-resolution orthographic protocol. On 1,000 shared episodes, it achieves 50.0% versus 27.9% for the strongest adapted baseline using the same model, prior, sensing stack, and movement budget. Observation-based verification by the Examiner contributes 5.9 points of this success, and at a reduced reasoning-effort setting WORLDS still exceeds the adapted GeoNav baseline by 18.8 points while generating fewer tokens. We also demonstrate WORLDS on a quadrotor, which flies the generated sensing waypoints and grounds three language targets, including a vehicle absent from the map, from its onboard imagery.

title: Robust Machine Learning Handling Noise, Bias and Adversarial Attacks
abstract: range of applications, including healthcare, finance, cybersecurity, autonomous systems, communication networks, and other data-driven environments. However, the increasing deployment of machine learning models in real-world and high-stakes applications has revealed important challenges related to noisy data, uncertainty, biased information, distributional changes, model vulnerabilities, and adversarial manipulation. These challenges highlight the need for machine learning systems that are not only accurate but also reliable, secure, resilient, and trustworthy. The book Robust Machine Learning: Handling Noise, Bias and Adversarial Attacks presents a comprehensive discussion of the principles, methodologies, challenges, and applications associated with developing robust machine learning systems. The book begins with the foundations of robust machine learning, introducing the concepts of robustness, generalization, uncertainty, data quality, and the major sources of vulnerability in conventional machine learning models. It establishes the importance of designing models capable of maintaining stable performance when exposed to noisy inputs, distribution shifts, incomplete information, and adversarial perturbations. These foundational aspects provide readers with a clear understanding of why robustness has become a fundamental requirement for trustworthy artificial intelligence. The subsequent chapters examine the effects of noise and imperfect information on statistical learning systems. Particular attention is given to different forms of noise, including feature noise, label noise, and adversarial perturbations, together with their influence on model performance and generalization. The book also addresses data quality and preprocessing, covering missing values, noisy and corrupted data, outlier detection, data cleaning, normalization, transformation, and data integration. These discussions emphasize the importance of high-quality and representative data in developing reliable machine learning models. Bias and fairness represent another important dimension of robust machine learning. The book examines different sources of bias, including data, algorithmic, human, measurement, and deployment bias, together with methods for detecting and mitigating unfair outcomes. Fairness criteria, evaluation approaches, pre-processing, in-processing, post-processing, adversarial debiasing, and responsible AI considerations are discussed to highlight the relationship between robustness, fairness, transparency, and ethical machine learning. A major focus of the book is robust optimization and adversarial machine learning. The chapters explore robust optimization principles, uncertainty sets, min-max formulations, adversarial training, distributionally robust optimization, and uncertainty-aware learning. Adversarial machine learning is examined through threat models and attack strategies, including evasion, poisoning, and backdoor attacks. The book further discusses defense mechanisms such as adversarial training, defensive distillation, input transformation, detection mechanisms, certified robustness, and randomized smoothing. These topics provide a systematic perspective on the security challenges faced by modern machine learning systems. The book also addresses the growing importance of explainability and interpretability in robust machine learning. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), model interpretability, feature attribution, visualization, LIME, SHAP, counterfactual explanations, and the relationship between explainability and robustness are explored. The discussion emphasizes that trustworthy AI requires not only resilient models but also systems whose decisions can be understood, evaluated, and appropriately governed. Modern deep learning architectures are considered through a dedicated discussion of robust neural network design and regularization. Convolutional Neural Networks, Recurrent Neural Networks, transformer-based architectures, residual connections, gating mechanisms, dropout, L1/L2 regularization, label smoothing, Mixup, CutMix, stochastic depth, robust loss functions, and adversarial training are examined as approaches for improving resilience against noise, corruption, overfitting, and distributional changes. The book further extends robustness to federated and distributed learning environments, where data and computation are decentralized. It examines data and model poisoning, Byzantine failures, privacy leakage, secure aggregation, differential privacy, secure multi-party computation, and homomorphic encryption, while also considering scalability, communication efficiency, heterogeneity, edge computing, and IoT environments. Evaluation and benchmarking are also given significant attention. Robust machine learning cannot be assessed solely through conventional accuracy measures. Accordingly, the book considers robustness metrics, adversarial evaluation, stress testing, distributional shifts, calibration, uncertainty estimation, benchmark datasets, reproducibility, standardization, and multi-metric evaluation. Such approaches are essential for determining whether a model can maintain reliable performance beyond controlled experimental conditions. The final chapter brings these concepts into practical perspective by examining applications of robust machine learning in healthcare, finance, cybersecurity, autonomous systems, and other real-world environments. It highlights the importance of handling noisy and incomplete data, distributional shifts, adversarial manipulation, deployment constraints, explainability, fairness, and computational efficiency when building practical AI systems. Overall, this book is intended to serve as a useful reference for students, research scholars, academicians, machine learning practitioners, data scientists, cybersecurity professionals, and technology researchers interested in reliable and trustworthy artificial intelligence. By bringing together theoretical foundations, data-centric methods, optimization techniques, adversarial security, explainability, deep learning, decentralized learning, evaluation methodologies, and real-world applications, the book provides a holistic perspective on robust machine learning. The editors hope that this book will support readers in understanding the challenges of developing resilient machine learning systems and encourage further research, innovation, and responsible deployment of AI technologies in increasingly complex and dynamic environments.

title: Contract-Preserving Lower-to-Upper Recalibration in Hierarchical Agent Systems: An Integrated Framework
abstract: Soft and Hard De-Attraction (SHDA) specifies when verified lower-level recovery can support an upper-level revision without changing the external success contract. This condition is the framework's central axis, contract-preserving correctability: the joint condition, over separately judged coordinates, under which verified lower-level evidence may be admitted as the next correction and to which the system must return after each correction, containment, or revision. Because the components share budgets, strengthening one can break another; SHDA therefore organizes them as one closed loop along the axis, in which balance is an allocation of the shared budgets, not compensation. When a certified obligation fails, premise-level fault localization (T10) localizes the violation, within the recorded scope, to a false registered premise and its owner, a named record gap, or an unsound rule or checker; earliest failure sets diagnostic priority rather than establishing a causal mechanism. Under explicit assumptions, T1-T9 connect endogenous-error tracking, precision gates and probes, finite-phase progress, revision-aware certificate validity, transport between theorem epochs, repair costs, and same-episode outcomes. The scalar bounds and concentration tools are established ingredients; the proposed contribution is the integration layer: the objects, laws, and operations that exist only where the components meet. Three validation reports supply synthetic-loop tests (X3), planted-cause identification and fresh-audit repair comparisons (X2), and finite reachability checks (X1); their evidence is not interchangeable. In X2, certified full refresh matched budget-feasible diagnosis-guided repair in joint completion at nearly equal or lower cost, but a complete repair library and risk components with no failures observed in the retained runs left the repair value of diagnosis and risk untested; X1 separates post-fence compliance from safety under physical invalidation. The evidence supports scoped constructions and implementation obligations, not algorithmic superiority, deployed-agent safety, or unconditional convergence. Note on Version 2.0. This version replaces Version 1.0 (September 2026; about 9,200 words) and is a substantial revision (about 39,500 words). It organizes the framework around the contract-preserving correctability axis, adds premise-level fault localization (T10), states the conditional results as T1-T9, and adds three validation reports: finite reachability checks (X1), planted-cause identification and fresh-audit repair comparisons (X2) and synthetic-loop tests (X3). The Technical Supplement is revised as well (about 12,500 to 54,900 words). Files: the manuscript and the Technical Supplement as PDFs, and one supplement archive (132 files) with reproduction code, compact results and the validation reports. The Version 1.0 files remain available in the previous version of this record. Scope and status. This is the flagship of the Integrated Framework series on contract-preserving lower-to-upper recalibration (SHDA). The upload also contains the revised Technical Supplement, which states and proves T1-T9 and specifies the typed state, lineage, operations, attribution, disclosure and re-entry rules, the execution pipeline and the records. Companion A (residual genesis and dynamic feedback route attribution), Companion B (intervention-disclosure visibility and time-bounded selective nondisclosure), Companion C (family-scoped capability control, typed lineage and atomic re-entry) and the technical working paper SHDA Algorithms for Scoped Evidence Reuse and Recalibration are archived separately. The evidence consists of synthetic and finite-model checks; it does not establish deployed-agent safety or algorithmic superiority. AI use disclosure. Generative AI (GPT-6.0, OpenAI; Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic) was used substantively in preparing this work, including source comparison, drafting and editing, and, where applicable, mathematical and counterexample checks and the writing and running of supplementary code. The research questions, framework and final claims were directed and reviewed by the author, who takes full responsibility for the content, including the accuracy of all references and reported numbers. Repository metadata were prepared with assistance from Claude (Anthropic).

title: Beyond Encoder Fusion: Multi-View Discrete Token Augmentation for LLM-Based ASR
abstract: Discrete speech tokens provide a compact interface between speech encoders and large language models for automatic speech recognition, but single-tokenization systems remain sensitive to the chosen encoder. We propose multi-view discrete token augmentation, a simple strategy that augments each training utterance by generating alternative token sequences from fixed SSL encoders, such as HuBERT, WavLM, and MMS-300M. These tokenizations are treated as complementary training views for a shared LLM decoder, exposing it to more diverse discrete speech representations without requiring multi-encoder inference. At test time, the model can operate with a single encoder. On LibriSpeech, the approach consistently improves all encoders over independently trained baselines, with WavLM reaching 3.30% WER on test-clean and 8.13% on test-other. Budget-matched controls show that the gains come from encoder diversity rather than data volume. ROVER over multi-view hypotheses further improves WER to 3.03% and 7.38%.

title: dnalang stack 2026-09-20: dnalang-core, organism_sim, bridge — pre-registered results
abstract: Archival release of organism_sim, an artificial-life simulation of rule-evolving agents (XCS-lineage Learning Classifier System, closed s-expression action DSL from dna::}{::lang 0.2, routed message bus, hash-chained telemetry). Pure NumPy, seeded and deterministic; no hardware, no physical constants, no language model in the execution loop. This release adds two pre-registered positive results and their data: Substrate-Opt-2, which reduces 16-bit drift recovery from 8,750 to 6,000 trials per shift on 5/5 held-out seeds (population size N=4000 with tournament selection; the judged configuration is frozen as lcs.PARAMS16), and M3b, in which POET-style open-ended task generation reaches pooled ANNECS 35 vs 25 (ratio 1.40, 4/5 seeds) at 12-16 bits - reversing the same machinery's earlier documented FAIL at 6-10 bits. Two confounds in M3b are reported with the result: a width-coverage artifact in one auxiliary criterion, and the fact that the winning arm bundles curriculum with competence inheritance. The pre-registered ablation separating them (M3c, fresh seeds 70-74) found that both contribute: poet 32 / curriculum-only 29 / random 22 pooled ANNECS, the curriculum-alone criterion passing by a thin margin (ratio 1.32 on medians, 1.14 on means). Also included: the pre-registration of M7a (LLM-guided evolution of the learner's own operators against PARAMS16; not yet run) and a snapshot of dnalang-core 0.2.0, the unreleased dependency organism_sim requires. Seven of the eleven pre-registered experiments in this record are negative and are retained in full: offline and LLM-authored priors, specificity-matched priors (three independent samples), evolved regulatory genes (which exhibited specification gaming), concept drift, and a 55-point XCS grid that failed to move the same ceiling Substrate-Opt-2 later moved. Every criterion was committed to git before its run; evaluation seeds are disjoint from tuning seeds; the scorecard in README.md is generated from the files under results/ and guarded by a test.

title: INGLIZ–O‘ZBEK KOLLOKVIAL KORPUSINI YARATISHDA KO‘P QATLAMLI ANNOTATSIYA MODELI
abstract: The article proposes a multi-layer annotation model for an English–Uzbek corpus of colloquial units. Existing Uzbek national, parallel, morphological and syntactic resources and international multiword-expression corpora are reviewed to identify a gap in pragmatics-aware bilingual description. The proposed record combines an English expression, a short authentic context and an Uzbek functional equivalent with layers for form, source metadata, contextual meaning, pragmatic function, register, evaluative stance, participant relations, AI suggestions and expert decisions. A quality-control workflow based on independent checking, adjudication and licensing constraints is also outlined.

title: Why GLUs Work?
abstract: The Gated Linear Unit (GLU) and its variants, particularly SwiGLU, have become the de facto standard for feed-forward networks in modern Large Language Models (LLMs). Despite their widespread adoption, the fundamental mechanisms underlying their superior performance over plain MLP activations—and their occasional instability under depth scaling—remain poorly understood. Through extensive controlled experimentation across 350+ models, 7 depth scales, and 2 datasets, we demonstrate that the success of GLUs lies in their implicit quadratic self-gating behavior, where the Hadamard product induces an effective x² growth factor. We validate this hypothesis by using single-projection MLP variants—MLP-S10, MLP-Quadratic, and MLP-Squared-ReLU—which replicate the performance of full GLUs, confirming that quadratic amplification is the dominant driver of performance. Furthermore, we identify a critical structural flaw in existing gated designs: the down-projection weight w is left mathematically unguarded in the upstream gradients, leading to uncontrolled growth and divergence in deep networks. We derive this flaw formally and introduce Wal10 and Wal10-SiLU, GLU variants where the activation cap is applied after the down-projection. This simple architectural change introduces a shared sech²(·) factor in all gradients, providing an automatic, self-regulating brake that prevents runaway growth for all three matrices. Experiments across scales show that under normal training, Wal10 variants match the performance of SwiGLU. However, when subjected to extreme conditions in a 100L Transformer, Wal10 caps activation values and suppresses dangerous gradients, while SwiGLU and SiTU-GLU allow them to grow for all three matrices; thus, even with soft capping, SiTU-GLU fails to prevent activation blow-up. Our results suggest that Wal10 offers a reliable balance of expressivity and stability for deep neural networks.

title: PureTearsDropped/dual-nonlinear-glu: v0.1.0
abstract: Gated layers in transformers keep their value branch linear: SwiGLU is silu(W_g h) * (W_u h). Making both branches nonlinear is not a new design — it is the Gated Tanh Unit, which Dauphin et al. (2017) measured and rejected because both branches contribute a gradient downscaling factor, and the GLU → GEGLU → SwiGLU line descends from that rejection. On a synthetic teacher–student benchmark with a residual and a 1/sqrt(depth) branch initialisation, that rejection does not reproduce. The larger finding is about a different property. The proposed pair f and g, like max(ax,-b) and the identity, are all linear above zero, and it is that linear positive half which costs. Removing it from the gate — a plain b·tanh(a x/b) on both sides — is worth 1.5–5.9× in all four cells of two teachers by two value branches; removing it from the value branch is 1.0–3.0×, with one cell where it does nothing. The two changes are redundant rather than additive. This is the one effect that two teachers giving otherwise opposite accounts both support. A control separates the mechanism. A fixed tanh, with nothing learned, keeps most of the gain when the value branch is nonlinear but falls below SwiGLU when it is not, because it sits in its own linear region (median argument 0.378) while a learned gate drives itself into saturation (median 3.2). What the learned scale buys is the operating point, and that decides the outcome only when the gate is the sole nonlinearity. The saturated gate is not a sign function — that was tested and is wrong, at 3.70× — but a clamp costs only 1.19×, and training with the clamp from the start costs 9%, so the gate needs no transcendental at all. Also recorded. asinh in the value branch can be evaluated by polynomials alone, with segment boundaries taken from the measured argument distribution rather than from the shape of asinh, reproducing a trained network's loss to seven figures and costing 30× on a GPU, where it must not be used; the block's output is the mixed second derivative of an elementary potential F(u)G(v), which survives the both-sides form; initialising the residual branch at 1/sqrt(depth) outweighs every activation choice measured; curvature-aware ternary rounding was derived, corrected, and failed; and a benchmark checklist for detecting tasks that do not need depth. Corrections to v0.1.0 are recorded in place: two measured statements about GPU kernel cost, an inference-time substitution described as free that costs 4.4%, and a 2.1× gain attributed to the wrong one of two simultaneous changes.

title: A Hybrid Explanation Framework with Semantic Clustering for Public Communication Systems
abstract: The swift use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in public communication systems has significantly facilitated the processing of vast data sets, predictive analytics, and automated decision-making. However, as we increasingly depend on complex black-box models, it raises significant concerns regarding transparency, accountability, and public trust. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques such as SHAP and LIME provide feature-level explanations; nonetheless, these outputs are predominantly numerical, reliant on cases, and challenging for non-technical individuals to comprehend. This limitation is particularly challenging in public communication contexts, as interpretability must extend beyond technical clarity to encompass semantic coherence and collective comprehension. This research presents a Hybrid Explanation Framework utilizing Semantic Clustering for Public Communication Systems, integrating quantitative explanation methodologies with semantic aggregation tactics. The system features a multi-layer architecture that transforms prediction outputs into explanation vectors, projects them into an explanation space, and subsequently use semantic clustering to extract higher-order interpretability patterns. The proposed methodology integrates explanation vectors to identify the thematic structures underlying model decisions, distinguishing it from conventional XAI methods that emphasize singular explanations. This enables the transition from first-order interpretability ("why was this decision made?") to second-order interpretability ("what semantic patterns define these decisions?"). The study employed a qualitative-conceptual research methodology, utilizing thematic analysis, comparative model analysis, and conceptual synthesis to construct the framework. The results demonstrate that semantic clustering enhances interpretability consistency, facilitates user understanding, and strengthens perceived trust compared to instance-level explanations alone. The divergence between data clustering and explanation clustering demonstrates that statistical similarity does not necessarily imply similarity in decision-making, highlighting the importance of structural interpretability in AI governance. The suggested methodology improves XAI by integrating semantic and communicative components, offering a scalable solution for transparent AI-driven public discourse. This method enhances the accountability, comprehensibility, and reliability of AI systems in public spaces by linking mathematical models to human cognition.

title: PAR2COX: Survival-Informed Tensor Decomposition for Phenotyping and Risk Prediction from Irregular Longitudinal Data
abstract: Accurate risk prediction is crucial for clinical-decision making, intervention planning, treatment and transplant allocation. However, longitudinal clinical data are often irregular and subject to censoring. We propose PAR2COX, a joint framework that integrates PARAFAC2 decomposition with Cox proportional hazards model, using patient-specific latent factors as covariates in the likelihood. The proposed alternating optimization framework jointly estimates phenotypes and survival parameters, enabling survival-guided representation learning. PAR2COX accommodates both historical patients with observed outcomes and current patients whose outcomes remain unknown. Numerical experiments and a case study based on MIMIC-IV data demonstrate improved risk stratification compared with existing approaches, highlighting the value of survival-informed phenotype learning.

title: Contrastive Reasoning Path Optimization for Improving Logical Inference in Language Models
abstract: Large language models have achieved remarkable fluency across a wide range of tasks, yet their performance on multi-step logical inference remains uneven, brittle, and difficult to audit. This paper develops contrastive reasoning path optimization as a system-level framework for improving logical inference in language models by supervising the structure of intermediate reasoning trajectories rather than only the correctness of final answers. The framework treats reasoning as a searchable space of candidate paths, pairs successful and unsuccessful trajectories under controlled perturbations, and trains models to discriminate between them while preserving calibration and interpretability. The paper situates this approach within the broader literature on chain-of-thought prompting, preference optimization, and process supervision, and then examines the architectural, infrastructural, and institutional conditions required for reliable deployment. Particular attention is given to structural trade-offs between latency, verification cost, and accuracy; to the design of trace repositories with provenance and contamination controls; to failure modes such as unfaithful rationales and reward overoptimization; and to questions of fairness, accountability, and sustainability in large-scale socio-technical systems. The analysis concludes that contrastive path optimization is best understood not as a single training trick but as an infrastructure commitment that couples data governance, evaluation science, and deployment economics. Without corresponding investment in auditability and policy oversight, gains in measured reasoning accuracy risk remaining fragile and unevenly distributed across populations and domains.

title: When Machines Know Everything: Redesigning Education Around What AI Cannot Replace — An Open Adaptive Competency Education (OACE) Architecture Integrating Reliance-Aware Assessment into Competency-Graph Progression
abstract: The rapid, near-universal availability of generative artificial intelligence has quietly dismantled a load-bearing assumption of modern education: that the ability to produce a correct answer, unaided, is a reliable proxy for competence. When a free chatbot can solve, explain, and format the majority of tasks assigned in a conventional grade-ladder curriculum, the traditional coupling of assessment to information recall and reproduction becomes unstable. This paper argues that the appropriate response is neither to ban AI from education nor to treat it as an unqualified substitute for instruction, but to redesign the underlying architecture of how learners progress and how that progression is verified. We introduce Open Adaptive Competency Education (OACE), a design-science artifact that reorganizes learning around a competency graph rather than a fixed age-grade-subject ladder, and that embeds a reliance-aware progression mechanism: a formal logic by which a learner's documented pattern of tool dependence — measured using constructs adapted from the emerging AI-reliance and cognitive-offloading literature — becomes an explicit input into whether, when, and how a learner advances to the next competency node. This integration is, to our knowledge, novel: existing work independently addresses competency-graph curriculum structures, AI-reliance measurement, and assist-versus-test transfer effects, but no prior architecture connects reliance measurement directly to progression logic within a single implementable system.

title: Data-centric AI in disaster management: Scalable Named Entity Recognition via LLM-based stacking and pseudo-label generation
abstract: This study presents a scalable Teacher–Student architecture for Named Entity Recognition (NER) that enables automatic information extraction from Turkish disaster-related social media texts. To reduce labeling costs, the collective intelligence of three large language models (Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5) is combined through a learnable stacking meta-classifier. On a 500-tweet manually annotated dataset, stacking reached a token-level Macro F1 of 0.9313 (0.9219 under leakage-free tweet-level grouped cross-validation), on par with the strongest individual model (0.9245) and clearly above a BERT baseline trained on the same data (0.8335). It was selected as the Teacher for its learnable per-class weighting, its stability across meta-classifiers and its robustness to single-provider outages. The Teacher’s discrete predictions were transferred to a more efficient BERT Student through hard-label pseudo-labeling, and this Student was then used as a zero-cost proxy labeler to scale the corpus to 17,000 tweets. On a fully isolated 300-tweet blind test set, the final model obtained an entity-level Macro F1 of 0.9160, against 0.8648 for the baseline trained only on manual labels. A size-matched controlled experiment isolates the source of this gain: labeling the same 3000 tweets with the model ensemble instead of a self-training labeler improves entity-level Macro F1 by 0.033 in all five random seeds ( p < 0.001 ), whereas scaling from 3000 to 17,000 instances adds only 0.006. Label quality, rather than data volume, drives the improvement, and the approach offers a practical, low-cost route to rapid humanitarian needs mapping when annotated data is scarce.

title: Simultaneous Reduction of Observables and Measured Qudits in Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Local Recovery
abstract: For a general entanglement-assisted or unassisted quantum error-correcting code, a set of erasures, and an associated repair group, we propose a linear algebraic procedure to compute a reduced set of observables and a reduced repair group of codeword qudits for correcting the given erasures. The procedure has cubic complexity in the repair group size and the computed set of observables has the smallest possible size for correcting the given erasures. We specialize the general procedure to quantum codes constructed from Euclidean and Hermitian orthogonality, and provide closed-form upper bounds on the size of reduced repair groups for those special cases. Based on these closed-form bounds, we propose quantum counterparts of the information locality of classical local recovery.
